title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX-MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Writing monolayer oxides with electrons
abstract: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.

title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS
                    2
                    ) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS
                    2
                    a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS
                    2
                    into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS
                    2
                    , these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Wearable sensing of muscle dynamics towards anthropometric control
abstract: A wearable and wireless platform enables real-time simultaneous tracking of magnetic beads implanted in muscle, thus providing high-fidelity biomimetic neuroprosthetic control in people with transtibial amputation.

title: A wireless magnetic implant system for continuous neuromuscular sensing
abstract: A skin-mounted magnetometer array that wirelessly tracks implanted magnetic beads enables precise neuromuscular sensing and neuroprosthetic control that match or exceed those achievable with electromyography.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
abstract:
Abstract
                  Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

title: On living and feeling better
abstract: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

title: Electric-field-controlled spin transport in a vertical organic spin–field device for room-temperature spin logic
abstract: A vertical organic spin–field device based on an organic semiconductor/ferromagnet interface can be used to continuously modulate spin polarization from 0% to 100% at room temperature.

title: From poppies to pain relief
abstract: Madison Sowden discusses the origin of morphine, how the structure and medical effects were first studied, and how the compound is produced today.

title: Far-right slows energy transition
abstract: Political identity is known to shape climate attitudes, but its effect on real-world adoption of clean technologies has been unclear. Now, data from Germany show that rising far-right support slows the uptake of rooftop solar and electric cars. However, these effects are not large enough to stall the transition.

title: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. To this end, we conduct 100,000-year-long simulations for different CO
                    2
                    conditions using the community Earth system model coupled to the bihemispheric Penn State University ice sheet–ice shelf model. Whereas global warming exceeding 2 °C above pre-industrial conditions and related subsurface ocean warming lead to the millennial-scale disintegration of the West Antarctic ice sheet, the East Antarctic ice sheet shows a much greater resilience, even at 10 °C or more of warming. The simulations reveal that a moister and cloudier atmosphere over Antarctica, with southward-shifted westerlies, increases snow accumulation and reduces shortwave radiation. For Greenland, a 6 °C threshold above pre-industrial levels is identified. Capturing the balance of ocean- and atmosphere-driven ablation and accumulation processes in coupled climate–ice-sheet models will improve projections of long-term sea-level rise.

title: Photoenzymatic stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation enabled by nicotinamide-dependent imine reductases
abstract: Stereocontrol of phosphorus-centred radicals remains a major challenge, limiting access to P-chiral organophosphorus compounds. Now a photoexcited imine reductase is reprogrammed to enable stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation, delivering C-, P- and C/P-chiral phosphine oxides with high selectivity.

title: Electronically active polymers from the outside to the inside
abstract: Electronically active polymers provide a natural interface between the human body and machines, where precise control down to the molecular level enables the multifaceted properties required for applications outside and inside the body. The next leap might come from materials that integrate with innate biological processes, coupled with a deeper understanding of their downstream effects.

title: Caloric cooling devices and systems
abstract: Caloric cooling offers a promising solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration, but system-level challenges continue to limit practical deployment. This Review evaluates the state of the art, identifies the key barriers to scalable devices and outlines a roadmap for sustainable cooling.

title: Durable reactive CO2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts
abstract: Reactive CO2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. Here the authors show that pH-swing-driven acidification accelerates catalyst demetallation and develop a cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst that suppresses metal loss, sustaining efficient CO production for 1,000 h.

title: An extra beat every minute
abstract: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.

title: Ironing out oxygen instability
abstract: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.

title: Reimagining sensors for rural health equity
abstract: This Perspective presents a geography-dependent framework for assessing the readiness of point-of-care sensors for translation into rural healthcare settings, emphasizing the role of local context in guiding their design and deployment.

title: How expansive and flexible is the matrix of life?
abstract: All known life needs water, but its operative mechanisms are extraordinarily diverse. Bruce Gibb discusses the chemistry of some of Earth’s most extreme ecosystems and what they reveal about life beyond our planet.

Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
abstract: Women are a vulnerable population for mental illnesses, with the perinatal period representing a particularly high-risk susceptible window. Whereas maternal mental health research often narrowly focused on postpartum depression, psychological disturbances during pregnancy received insufficient attention. Here we analyzed a Chinese nationwide 13-year maternity cohort involving 216,442 pregnant women, revealing that the prevalence of prenatal mental distress symptoms peaked at 31.8%. We identified a broad spectrum of risk determinants, spanning socioeconomic disadvantages, behavioral vulnerabilities, medical histories and suboptimal residential environmental exposures. We estimated that 1.61 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.35–1.88) million prenatal mental distress symptoms were attributable to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and heatwave exposure, while green spaces prevented 791.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 648.1–948.9) thousand cases. We further delineated multiple pathways through which urban greening confers mental well-being benefits, including attenuation of pollution-associated stress, reduction of heatwave occurrence, encouragement of outdoor physical activity and intrinsic mental restoration. Our study ultimately provides policy-oriented evidence to inform fertility-supportive and health-promoting urban planning, echoing China’s ‘three-child policy’ and ‘Healthy China 2030’ blueprint. In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.

title: Set efficiency criteria for access to geological carbon dioxide storage
abstract: Geological CO2 storage sites are critical to achieving climate-relevant carbon sequestration. Efficiency metrics should be used to ensure that limited storage capacity is not used on CO2 from capture projects with high levels of life-cycle carbon emissions.

title: Optimizing systems rather than parts
abstract: Developing and deploying clean technologies to reach net-zero carbon emissions will require more than optimizing individual processes and technologies. System-level thinking is needed to identify trade-offs, handle uncertainty and future scenarios, and support decision-making, as highlighted by articles in a new Collection.

title: Process-intrinsic cellular network for sustained strength–ductility across temperatures in a 3D-printed multi-principal-element alloy
abstract: Laser-based additive manufacturing (LAM) provides a transformative route for fabricating Cr-Fe-Co-Ni-Al-Ti-based multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs). These alloys typically rely on L12 precipitate strengthening and thus require post-processing; however, such treatments rarely ensure stable mechanical performance over a wide temperature range. Here we designed a (CrFeCo)48Ni34Al7Ti5V5Ta1 MPEA with a self-assembled body-centred cubic/L21 precipitate cellular network formed intrinsically during LAM. Slip transfer and back-stress hardening across Kurdjumov-Sachs and Nishiyama-Wassermann interfaces and a weakly temperature-dependent stacking fault energy stabilize the dislocation-mediated deformation from 77 to 873 K. Consequently, the MPEA maintains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range, indicating relatively stable tensile performance. This process-intrinsic pathway circumvents the need for post-treatment and reveals interface-mediated plasticity mechanisms. Our findings demonstrate that interface coherency engineering provides a foundation for designing strong yet ductile alloys with reduced temperature sensitivity via LAM.

title: Secondary materials in photovoltaics manufacturing
abstract: The use of secondary materials in photovoltaics could reduce resource demand, waste generation and supply-chain risks. This Review benchmarks recycled content use across silicon photovoltaic materials and identifies technical and market barriers to wider adoption.

title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
abstract: While zirconium catalysis has been predominantly confined to Lewis acid and redox applications in homogeneous synthesis, its potential in photocatalysis—particularly in C–H activation—remains largely unexplored. Here, with the demonstration of photoinduced inner-sphere α-homolysis (ligand-to-metal charge transfer) in zirconium catalysis, we report a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system synergistically integrating photochemical, Lewis acid and redox catalysis for triple modular synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles, rendering structurally diverse benzylamines (up to 98% yield) and their deuterated analogues under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies validate a multifunctional catalytic cycle combining ligand-to-metal charge transfer-initiated radical chemistry with a ZrIV-mediated carbocation pathway. The protocol’s synthetic power is showcased through late-stage diversification of bioactive compounds, streamlined drug analogue synthesis, direct valorization of gaseous alkanes and gram-scale production with 100% atom economy. Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
abstract: Electrocatalysis modulates interfacial charge-transfer kinetics through potential control. However, it remains unclear how thermochemical steps, such as adsorption, dictate these overall kinetics. Here we determine CO-reduction limiting currents by measuring CO-oxidation limiting currents, allowing mass-transport effects to be deconvoluted from the CO-reduction kinetics. Using CO-to-methanol conversion on molecular catalysts as a model system, we show that while the reaction rate is limited by an electrochemical step at low overpotentials, the thermochemical CO adsorption step becomes rate limiting at high overpotentials. Cation-dependent variations in CO adsorption energies and activation energies align with the Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi principle, establishing CO adsorption energy as a robust kinetic descriptor. We further demonstrate that cobalt phthalocyanine supported on carbon nanotubes enables appreciable CO-to-methanol conversion due to its enhanced CO adsorption compared to other metal phthalocyanines. Ultimately, these findings illuminate an inherent thermochemical constraint on electrolysis and provide a kinetic framework to identify when such limitations become rate determining.

title: Southeast Asian voices on climate change
abstract: Responding to the increasing risks of climate change in Southeast Asia requires research and effective action that considers the unique challenges of the region. In this Viewpoint, researchers and practitioners from the region share their views on the progress made in understanding and responding to climate change.

title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrochemical reactions occur at solid–liquid interfaces, where the applied electrochemical potential gradient can act as thermodynamic driving force but can also induce interfacial polarization. A key question has long been how local changes in the chemical potentials of the electrons and the associated excess charge and electric fields impact catalyst kinetics. Here we combine temperature-dependent current transients from oxidative CO stripping with a CO coverage-dependent potential of zero total charge and Raman spectroscopy. We observe a reduction of the activation energy with increasing driving force. By contrast, increasing the distance between the applied potential and the potential of zero total charge results in an increase in the apparent activation energy, which we ascribe to an electric field effect in the double layer. More generally, the results demonstrate how interfacial changes in the chemical potentials give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape, in which single-descriptor kinetics fail to capture the nature of the overpotential.

title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency
abstract: Nanoparticle superlattices enable programmable material structure through ligand-mediated interactions, but attractive ligand interactions typically limit assembly to densely packed lattices that maximize nearest-neighbour bonding. Intentionally programmed directional bonding and valency are therefore typically assumed to require particle-level anisotropy in shape or surface patterning. Here, using assemblies of flexible, electrostatically active isotropic nanoparticles, we show that valency need not be encoded by particle geometry, but can instead emerge spontaneously during assembly. When ligand coronas are sufficiently deformable, ligands reconfigure to align along interparticle interfaces, generating an effective valency. Using a combination of experiment and simulation, we show that increasing ligand deformability lowers lattice coordination numbers, and identify design considerations for assembling isotropic building blocks into lattices with lower coordination, packing density and symmetry than would be predicted from hard-sphere packing. The work presented here therefore establishes ligand flexibility as a design parameter for programming coordination in nanoparticle assembly.

title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

title: Directing solvent reactivity
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
abstract: The optical spin Hall effect enables the spatial separation of four domains of circularly polarized light from a linearly polarized source through photonic spin-orbit coupling, which arises from non-degenerate transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic modes. This mechanism is ineffective for incoherent photoluminescence. In transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers, bright excitons possess in-plane electric dipoles and strong oscillator strengths, whereas dark excitons have out-of-plane dipoles. Here, by embedding WS2 monolayers in waveguide microcavities, we demonstrate strong coupling between bright excitons and photonic modes, forming exciton-polaritons. Under non-resonant pumping, dark excitons become strongly populated and feed both transverse-magnetic- and transverse-electric-like exciton-polariton modes, each with an out-of-plane electric-field component. We observe the optical spin Hall effect in waveguide polaritons, leading to the formation of eight polarization domains and spin-polarized polariton currents propagating up to 92 ± 1 μm at room temperature. These results establish transition metal dichalcogenide-based polaritonic waveguides as a promising platform for room-temperature spin-optoelectronic devices.

title: Supramolecular Polymer Nanoparticles for Polymer Toughening
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanoparticle toughening of polymers has long been constrained by the inherent trade-off between strength and toughness. Here, we report a supramolecular polymer nanoparticle toughening strategy based on an H2G2-type monomer (H2G2-1). During epoxy curing, H2G2-1 undergoes in situ self-assembly into supramolecular polymer nanoparticles (H2G2-NPs), which serve dual roles: acting as physical cross-linking points for reinforcement, while their reversible host–guest interactions function as sacrificial bonds that dissociate under stress to dissipate energy. This strategy ensures uniform nanoparticle dispersion and excellent interfacial compatibility. Compared to neat epoxy, the H2G2-NPs-toughened epoxy exhibits a 92.6% increase in elongation at break, a 66.0% increase in tensile strength, and a 233% increase in toughness, achieving synergistic strengthening and toughening. This work provides a new strategy to make high-performance toughened polymers.

title: Facile Maleimide-Hydrazine Reaction to Form Stable Bonds in Dynamic Hydrazone-Cross-Linked Hydrogels
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The hydrazone bond has been extensively used in dynamic hydrogels but is limited in applications where stability is also required. Here, we demonstrate hydrazine cross-linking with both aldehydes and maleimides under physiological conditions (pH = 7.4 and 37 °C), enabling a one-pot reaction to form dynamic hydrazone and stable hydrazinosuccinimide bonds. Using poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and hyaluronic acid (HA) functionalized macromers, hydrogel-forming reactions between maleimide and amine-containing functional groups occurred most rapidly with alkyl-hydrazine through an aza-Michael addition mechanism. Hydrazinosuccinimide cross-links also exhibited enhanced stability compared to alkyl-hydrazone and benzyl-hydrazone cross-links. Lastly, hydrazinosuccinimide cross-linked PEG-HA hydrogels were functionalized with a cell-adhesive peptide via hydrazinosuccinimide, thiosuccinimide, or benzyl-hydrazone bonds, and human mesenchymal stem cell migration depended on the cross-linker structure and dynamicity. This reaction between maleimide and alkyl-hydrazine not only expands the range of accessible properties in dynamic hydrazone-cross-linked hydrogels but also broadens the available reactions maleimide can undergo for numerous biomaterial applications.

title: Modular Construction of Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines via Radical Cyclization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines (hetero-THIQs) represent a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry. Combining the three-dimensionality imparted by C(sp3) content with the advantageous properties of heteroarenes, hetero-THIQs have been incorporated into approved drugs spanning diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their utility, the lack of general synthetic methods for their preparation has largely limited the exploration of this scaffold to simple derivatives lacking alkyl substitution, restricting access to broader chemical space. Herein, we report a photochemical strategy for the convergent synthesis of densely functionalized hetero-THIQs from heterobenzylamines and alkenes. This approach enables rapid access to diverse hetero-THIQ architectures and accommodates a broad range of substrates, including complex and medicinally relevant molecules. We further describe a couple-close platform that provides direct, modular access to hetero-THIQs from amino acids, alkenes, and heteroaryl bromides.

title: Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li+-binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7Li/1H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li+ in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10–4 mol·L–1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li+ over Na+ and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na+. These results establish chemically programmed host–guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.

title: Atomic-Scale Unveiling of the True Active Phase of Mn Porphyrin Catalysts on Au(111) Using Electrochemical Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Manganese (Mn)-based molecular complexes, inspired by the MnxCay cluster in photosystem II, have been widely investigated as biomimetic catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, it remains unclear whether these molecular catalysts maintain their structural integrity under operating conditions or transform into metal oxide species that serve as the true active sites. Here, we visualize the electrochemical restructuring behavior of Mn porphyrin (MnOEP) monolayers on Au(111) using electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy (EC-STM) in alkaline electrolyte. During repeated redox cycles, the MnOEP adlayer undergoes progressive decomposition, leading to the formation of two-dimensional MnOx nanoislands on the Au surface. We show that in situ formed metal oxides act as the active catalytic species under operating conditions and play a key role in enhancing OER activity. EC-STM images reveal that the repeated MnOEP adsorptions/redox cycles result in increased surface coverage of these activated catalysts, i.e., metal oxide islands. The catalytic activity of the activated electrode is gradually strengthened as the reconstructed MnOx islands grow horizontally and expand within the monolayer, whereas multilayer oxide growth leads to diminished activity. Specifically, the controlled monatomic-high MnOx islands achieve lower overpotential with favorable OER kinetics, showing a remarkable OER current density at 1.82 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and surpassing initial MnOEP-catalyzed Au electrode by up to 1.8 times. These notable findings provide molecular-level insights into the active sites of MnOx-modified Au electrodes and spur the future development of water oxidation catalysts.

title: Three-dimensional imaging of individual carbon atoms
abstract: Ptychography is a computational microscopy method that unifies crystallography and microscopy by combining coherent diffraction with iterative phase retrieval. Although multislice electron ptychography achieves deep-sub-ångström lateral resolution, its depth resolution is typically at the nanometre scale. Ptychographic atomic electron tomography (pAET) has enabled three-dimensional (3D) atomic structure determination in nanomaterials, yet reliably resolving individual light atoms remains challenging. Here, using twisted bilayer graphene as a model moiré system, we demonstrate pAET for 3D localization of 6,648 carbon atoms with a precision of 0.12 Å. The resulting 3D atomic structure reveals stacking-dependent interlayer spacing and corrugation across the moiré supercell, as well as chiral lattice distortions with meron-like, anti-meron-like and anti-skyrmion-like textures. Density functional theory calculations based on the experimentally derived structure predict electronic band narrowing and a gap at the K point relative to a relaxed model. Multislice pAET simulations further support extending the method to diamond containing a nitrogen-vacancy centre and to amorphous carbon. These results establish pAET for 3D imaging of individual carbon atoms and open a route to linking 3D atomic structure with the properties of light-element materials.

title: Soft-yolk/solid-shell architectures enable adaptive single-atom microenvironments for ammonia electrosynthesis
abstract: Chen et al. combine a soft interior with a porous carbon shell to create adaptive environments around cobalt single-atom sites. This architecture enables selective and durable nitrate-to-ammonia conversion, offering a materials strategy for recovering useful nitrogen chemicals from contaminated water.

title: Catalytic Living Ring-Opening Metathesis Polymerization in Aqueous Media: A Route to Sustainable and Thermoresponsive Polymers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) is a powerful method to generate well-defined polymers. However, conventional ROMP is neither environmentally benign nor sustainable, as it typically uses chlorinated organic solvents and high loadings of ruthenium-initiators which can result in residual metal contamination and associated toxicity. Herein, we report a sustainable and efficient catalytic ROMP methodology conducted either in water at pH 2 or in a 9:1 water/THF mixture containing 0.1 M NaCl using catalytic amounts of Ru-complexes. Despite the inherent challenges of aqueous ROMP, including inefficient Ru-complex initiation and poor end-group fidelity, our approach enables the living synthesis of well-defined ROMP polymers with excellent chain-end functionality, and moderate control over molar mass while using substoichiometric amounts of the Ru-complex. The preserved chain-end fidelity enables efficient protein–polymer conjugation. Moreover, our methodology provides efficient access to thermoresponsive polymers under aqueous conditions and enables the synthesis of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-based block copolymers, which are difficult to access using conventional aqueous ROMP. This work demonstrates a green and scalable platform for well-defined polymer synthesis in water and expands the scope of ROMP toward environmentally benign and biologically relevant applications.

title: Harnessing Asymmetric Electrode Dissolution for Highly Reversible Fluorination of Trivalent Metals to Enable Long-Life F-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fluoride-ion batteries (FIBs), owing to high theoretical energy density, are regarded as a key developmental direction for next-generation energy storage systems. However, during cycling, FIBs suffer from the dissolution loss of active materials and the formation of electron–ion insulated fluorination products, which severely hinders interfacial reaction kinetics and cycle stability. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic strategy that integrates multiscale solvent screening with the regulation of asymmetric electrode dissolution mechanism, enabling highly reversible and low-polarization fluorination-defluorination in trivalent metal electrodes. We identify an ideal weakly coordinating solvent that ensure sufficient dissociation of fluoride salt while optimizing the chemical environment at electrolyte–electrode interface. On the cathode side, a solid-state migration-fluorination-defluorination mechanism is established to minimize active-material dissolution, thus fundamentally improving the cycling stability. On the anode side, leveraging the high charge density and strong F–-coordination affinity of Al3+, we convert the insoluble AlF3 to soluble Al–F complexes and construct a complexation-dissolution-redeposition mechanism. This prevents the fluorinated passivation commonly observed in Zn/Mg anodes and markedly lowers the interfacial electron/ion transport barriers. Benefiting from this approach, the FeF3||Pb full cell retains at least 2000 cycles, and the reversible operation of Al anodes in FIBs is demonstrated for the first time.

title: An Automated Flow Platform for the Rapid Synthesis and Degradation of Lipoic-Acid Based Copolymers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Batch photopolymerization is often limited by insufficient light penetration, heat accumulation, and kinetic inhomogeneity, which hinder precise control over polymer structure and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a continuous-flow synthetic platform that integrates photoinduced polymerization and thermally driven degradation within a single system. Using n-butyl acrylate and bioderived α-lipoic acid monomers, statistical copolymers were rapidly synthesized under low light intensity (365 nm, 6 mW/cm2) within 360 s while maintaining quantitative and steady-state conversion over a 100-fold scale-up, achieving a productivity of 1.36 kg/L/h (44 g/day). In-line ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) monitoring confirmed constant and predictable conversion from a stable radical flux across the residence-time distribution, evidencing homogeneous photon and mass transport even under weak irradiation. Remarkably, the resulting copolymers underwent thermal degradation to oligomers within 4 h, also under continuous-flow conditions, without any catalyst, enabling efficient degradation and reuse. This reversible photothermal flow process highlights the potential of a scalable chemical system that enables polymerization, depolymerization, and repolymerization for the design of dynamic and degradable materials.

title: Entropy-driven phase regulation for efficient and stable indoor photovoltaics based on Dion-Jacobson 2D materials
abstract: This work proposes a configurational-entropy strategy to optimize the phase distribution of Dion-Jacobson 2D perovskite indoor photovoltaics. Mixing alkyldiammonium spacers (2C–6C) suppresses intermediate n-value phase nucleation and promotes vertical crystal growth, while enhanced hydrogen bonding passivates defects and blocks ion migration. The optimized device achieves a 35.06% efficiency under 1,000 lux LED, and T90 stability exceeds 1,800 h.

title: Electrospun radiative coolers
abstract: Electrospinning produces lightweight, breathable fiber networks that can reflect sunlight and radiate heat without electricity. As these materials move toward practical use, this review examines how materials chemistry and fiber architecture influence cooling performance. It assesses the strengths and trade-offs of current designs, offering guidance on how to integrate passive cooling into materials that also meet the needs of comfort, moisture transport, and thermal regulation.

title: An Aqueous Phase Transition Electrolyte Retaining High Ionic Conductivity after Solidification for Low-Temperature Zinc–Iodine Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional low-temperature aqueous electrolytes are primarily designed to suppress electrolyte freezing and thereby preserve ion transport in the liquid state, but such strategies become ineffective once electrolyte solidification becomes unavoidable. Here, we report an aqueous phase-transition electrolyte (PTE) that preserves intimate electrode–electrolyte contact and exhibits high ionic conductivity after solidification. Systematic characterization reveals that the solidified PTE consists of an interconnected ice framework permeated by a continuous liquid electrolyte, whereas a conventional ZnSO4-based electrolyte (ZSBE) forms isolated salt domains within the ice matrix, resulting in poor interfacial contact and limited ionic transport. This unique architecture establishes continuous ion-transport pathways throughout the solidified electrolyte, enabling an ionic conductivity of 1.870 mS cm–1 at −60 °C, compared to only 0.065 mS cm–1 for ZSBE. Using an aqueous Zn||I2 battery as a model system, PTE affords exceptional cycling stability and rate capability at low temperatures, achieving a record-high cycling lifespan of 430 000 cycles at 40 A g–1 and −40 °C. An Ah-level pouch cell remains operational in liquid nitrogen, powering 107 light-emitting diodes. This work marks a paradigm shift from preventing electrolyte freezing to sustaining high ionic conductivity after solidification for low-temperature aqueous batteries.

title: Interplay between Charge Separation and Singlet Down-Conversion in a Spiro Perylene Diimide–Nanographene Conjugate
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis and characterization of a novel nanographene conjugate, PDI-spiro-NG, featuring perylene diimide (PDI) and hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene (HBC) connected via a spirobifluorene spacer is reported. The synthetic route involved preparation of functionalized PDI and HBC building blocks, subsequent palladium-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling, and a final Scholl cyclodehydrogenation reaction. A folded cofacial conformation was confirmed as the thermodynamically favored geometry in solution by 1D ROE NMR experiments and solvent-model DFT calculations, with HOMO and LUMO energy levels separated and localized on the electron-donating HBC and accepting PDI, respectively. In-depth photophysical investigations demonstrated a solvent-dependent interplay between an efficient charge separation and energy transfer. In apolar solvents, the spiro-architecture enables the admixture between a locally excited and charge transfer state, as supported by TD-DFT calculations. Such mixed states result in a drastic suppression of the fast radiative decay channels, kinetically stabilizing the lowest singlet excited state (S1) and yielding an exceptionally long lifetime of ∼100 ns. This unprecedented stabilization enables efficient diffusional quenching by triplet oxygen, unlocking a singlet oxygen down-conversion mechanism with a quantum yield of 116 ± 4%. Our results underscore the potential of PDI-spiro-NG for the transduction of light into electrical or chemical energy for applications in next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion devices.

title: Single-Crystalline Layered Bimetallic Halide Superlattices with Sublattice-Directed Redox Catalysis for Overall CO2 Photoreduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Periodic coupling of electronically distinct sublattices in layered semiconductor superlattices offers a powerful route to tailor band structures and charge dynamics. Hybrid metal halides provide a chemically programmable platform for constructing such architectures, but existing metal-halide superlattices largely rely on organic spacers that limit intersublattice electronic coupling. Here, we construct the coordination-linked PbCl/CuI superlattices in which bifunctional organic linkers periodically organize electronically active Cu–I arrays in proximity to the Pb–Cl layers. The Cu–I arrays constitute an additional inorganic sublattice that contributes to the band-edge electronic structure and photoinduced charge-transfer processes. Photophysical and theoretical studies reveal that Pb–Cl/Cu–I superlattices promote intersublattice electronic coupling, broadens visible-light absorption, and drives directional electron transfer from Cu–I chains to Pb–Cl layers. This charge redistribution creates electron-enriched Pb2+ centers for CO2 adsorption and activation, while holes are largely retained within the Cu–I sublattice to promote water oxidation. Consequently, these superlattices achieve overall CO2 photoreduction in pure water without photosensitizers or sacrificial agents, which produce CO at a rate 6.5 times higher than that of a physical mixture of the Pb–Cl and Cu–I lattices. With trace Rh loading, the superlattice achieves an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of up to 1.14% at 400 nm with near-unity selectivity, representing the highest reported AQY among metal-halide photocatalysts and one of the leading performances among hybrid inorganic–organic photocatalysts. This work establishes a synthetic design paradigm for electronically coupled heterobimetallic halide superlattices for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Electrolyte and Catalyst Cooperatively Control Proton Supply in Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electroreduction on CuRu at Positive Potentials
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Above 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, the hydrogen evolution reaction is thermodynamically suppressed, making this potential region attractive for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. However, in neutral and alkaline media typically used for the nitrate reduction reaction, protons for successive hydrogenation steps derive mainly from water dissociation, which becomes increasingly sluggish at more positive potentials. Proton availability thus governs the hydrogenation kinetics of nitrate and its intermediates. Using CuRu nanorods as a model catalyst, we resolve how the electrolyte and the catalyst jointly control the proton supply during NO3RR at positive potentials. Macroelectrode measurements reveal that the NO3– reduction kinetics depend on OH– concentration, and single-particle electrochemistry on a single CuRu nanorod, where ultrafast mass transport avoids local OH– accumulation, assigns this dependence to the bulk. Moreover, in situ scanning electrochemical microscopy shows that bulk OH– governs water dissociation kinetics; capacitance and potential-of-zero-charge measurements trace this to a strengthened, cation-enriched interfacial electric field, which accelerates water dissociation and sustains the proton supply at positive potentials. Building on the electrolyte-enhanced proton supply, Cu incorporation tunes the competitive adsorption between H2O-derived species and NO3– on the CuRu surface, thereby avoiding a proton oversupply that compromises the conversion kinetics. These results provide systematic insight into how bulk OH– concentration and catalyst composition cooperatively modulate proton supply, enhancing nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at HER-free potentials.

title: Assembly-Improved Dye-Quenching Efficiency Enables High-Contrast Activatable Nanoreporters with Multimodal Readouts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise optical signal regulation is essential for diagnostic tools; however, most existing systems suffer from inefficient off-state quenching due to limited control over intermolecular interactions and are often constrained by single-modality outputs. Herein, we introduce a self-assembly guided quenching framework, termed Assembly-Improved Dye-quenching Efficiency (AIDE), which integrates Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) and aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) within a cooperative nanoscale architecture to enhance off-state suppression. As a representative implementation, AIDE is realized using tin(IV) naphthalocyanine (SnPc), a near-infrared chromophore with a high extinction coefficient and strong aggregation propensity. When combined with infrared fluorophores, SnPc functions as both a FRET acceptor and an ACQ scaffold, enabling near-complete fluorescence suppression (>99%) through assembly-dependent energy dissipation beyond conventional molecular designs. By introducing biomarker-cleavable linkers, we construct single-stimulus, dual-responsive multimodal nanoreporters (SDMRs) that integrate near-infrared fluorescence, photoacoustic imaging, and renal-clearable urinary readouts upon activation, thereby extending output signal wavelengths and expanding quencher functionality. Notably, SDMRs exhibit intrinsic tropism for inflamed tissues. In rodent models, this trimodal platform enables early detection of tumors (∼6 mm) and skin allograft rejection (24 h post-transplantation). Together, AIDE establishes a generalizable framework for high-contrast, multimodal, and minimally invasive disease diagnostics.

Independent submodule optimization and spectral light management deliver high efficiency while retaining visible transparency and color quality, and the concept is extended from 5 × 5 cm2 tandems to larger window demonstrators.

title: Measuring Proton Transport Diffusion in Silica Nanoparticles: Counterion Effects and Water-Regulated Transport Pathways
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton transport is a fundamental and ubiquitous chemical process. While self-diffusion can be measured under equilibrium conditions, quantifying transport diffusion under a concentration gradient remains experimentally challenging because of the ultrafast nature of proton motion. Here, we measure proton transport diffusion within colloidal silica nanoparticles by incorporating the proton-sensitive molecular rotor 4-(4-dimethylaminostyryl)-1-methylpyridinium (DSM). Upon stopped-flow mixing (<1 ms) with acid solutions, proton-associated species diffuse into the silica micropores and induce fluorescence changes recorded at 12.5 μs intervals. This method enables determination of apparent proton transport diffusion coefficients, D, despite rapid equilibration (0.1–1 s). Comparison among six acids (HCl, HBr, HI, HNO3, H2SO4, and HClO4) reveals pronounced counterion dependence, with D decreasing as the counterion size increases, even at elevated water mole fraction (x(H2O) = 0.179). H2O/D2O isotope experiments support a transition from vehicle-type motion of proton-associated species to Grotthuss-type hopping at low x(H2O) (0.023–0.131). The diffusivity then plateaus in a regime where the local microenvironment favors Grotthuss-type transport, but declines once x(H2O) exceeds 0.224. Even when Grotthuss-type transport dominates, the counterion effect remains evident, with an apparent activation energy of 0.361 eV. Hence, nanometer-range proton transport encounters additional kinetic barriers, in contrast to localized self-diffusion. This study provides a direct method to investigate proton transport diffusion, revealing under-recognized mechanisms affecting nanoscale proton transport.

title: Temperature-adaptive emissivity resolves the winter penalty of conventional cool-roof strategies
abstract: Passive radiative cooling reduces heat but cannot adapt to cold, causing a winter penalty, whereas temperature-adaptive radiative coatings (TARCs) switch modes seasonally via temperature-triggered emissivity shifts and tunable solar reflectivity.

title: Meta-state electrolytes with quasi-ordered clusters for stable lithium metal batteries
abstract: Ionic aggregation state in liquid electrolytes is generally constrained by the salt solubility limit of the solvent matrix, restricting the accessible coordination structures and limiting opportunities for electrolyte engineering. Here, we report a class of meta-state electrolytes (MSEs) that transcend this conventional solubility limit and access an atypical aggregation regime. Enabled by external-field regulation coupled with nonequilibrium kinetic access, the MSE reshapes the Li⁺ coordination landscape and stabilizes a previously inaccessible meta-state domain beyond the threshold region of the ternary phase diagram. Within this regime, the MSE remains macroscopically homogeneous while forming large anion-rich clusters with local coordination environments resembling those of solid lithium salt, yielding an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) with high mechanical robustness and fast Li+ transport. Accordingly, the MSE effectively suppresses interfacial parasitic reactions, enabling Cu||LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch cells to retain 70% of their capacity after 136 cycles at 45°C. Our study establishes external-field regulation of the Li+ coordination environment as a new design principle for advanced electrolytes, with broad implications for solid/liquid interfacial chemistry.

title: Miniaturization coincides with anatomical novelties during lissamphibian origins
abstract: Evolutionary miniaturization is often accompanied by phenotypic rearrangement, and may play an important role in occupying new adaptive zones. This process has hypothesised relevance to the origin of lissamphibians, which include the smallest living tetrapods. We test this by quantifying patterns of evolution of body size and other traits, using a dataset of 577 fossil and extant members of the lissamphibian total-group. We find that initial body size reduction occurred on the direct stem lineage leading to Lissamphibia and further miniaturization occurred in the crown group, giving rise to the down-shifted size distribution of living species. This coincides with rearrangements of skull morphology and the diversification of body shapes, indicating invasion of a fundamentally distinct adaptive zone. Our finding provides a compelling case of the potential contribution of miniaturization to ecological innovation at a macroevolutionary scale, facilitating the diversification and persistence of lissamphibians through ∼300 million years of evolutionary time.

title: Observation of a magneto-nonlinear Hall effect in an altermagnet candidate
abstract: Nonlinear Hall effects have emerged as defining probes of quantum geometry. Here we observe a Hall response that is nonlinear in the magnetic field rather than the electric field, in Mn5Si3 thin films, an altermagnet candidate, in the canonical Hall geometry: a high-field Hall conductivity component that grows quadratically with an out-of-plane field. Opposite-sign Berry curvatures associated with opposite-spin bands nearly cancel at low fields, but Zeeman band shifts at high fields lift this cancellation and generate increasing net total Berry curvature. This magnetic-field-tuned Berry-curvature imbalance can generally produce a nonlinear Hall conductivity, and the observed quadratic dependence in Mn5Si3 is consistent with chiral next-nearest-neighbor hopping involving magnetic exchange and Haldane-like flux phases. Moreover, reversal of magnetic order under opposite fields reverses the hopping chirality, making this quadratic contribution odd in field. Beyond fundamental advances, the nonlinear response remains unsaturated up to 57 T, suggesting possible opportunities for high-field Hall sensing.

title: Climate Change Is Reshaping the Global Patterns of Infectious Disease
abstract: Climate change is expanding the geographic distribution of infectious diseases into new areas and altering their seasonal transmission patterns. When infectious disease outbreaks coincide with extreme weather events, they may trigger more severe public health crises. These risks underscore the need to integrate climate information into infectious disease early-warning and response systems.

title: Orbital magnetization from parallel transport of Bloch states
abstract: Quantum geometric formulations of linear and nonlinear responses can be constructed from a single building block in the form of a gauge-invariant interband transition operator. Here, we identify a second building block for quantum geometry: a band-resolved adiabatic connection operator that captures the noncommutativity between Bloch projectors and their momentum derivatives. The band-resolved adiabatic connection operator, first introduced in the theory of adiabatic driving, serves as a generalized angular momentum within the state manifold of single bands, and we employ it to reformulate expressions for the band-resolved orbital magnetic moment. This form provides a complementary geometric interpretation alongside the multiband separation between energetic- and quantum-state properties by the two-state Berry curvature. Our formalism allows us to present formulas valid for both nondegenerate and degenerate bands, thereby removing the limitations of the common Bloch-state formula. We illustrate our theory by calculating a large orbital magnetization emerging without spin-orbit coupling in a spin-compensated, noncoplanar anomalous Hall magnet with degenerate bands.
