title: Organocatalytic Enantiodifferentiation of Two Aryl Groups with Similar Steric Hindrances: Construction of gem ‐Diaryl Acyclic Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT Enantiodifferentiation of two aryl groups with similar steric hindrances is challenging. Although reactions involving diaryl ketones, diaryl alkenes, diaryl imines, diaryl carbenes, and diaryl radicals as substrates or intermediates have been reported for this purpose, successful enantiodifferentiation via diaryl conjugated carbanion intermediates has yet to be achieved. Moreover, existing methodologies predominantly rely on transition‐metal catalysis and are largely limited to the construction of gem ‐diaryl tertiary stereocenters, with no examples reported for the construction of gem ‐diaryl acyclic quaternary stereocenters. In this study, we have developed a phase‐transfer catalyst enabled enantiodifferentiation of two aryl groups with similar steric hindrances via diaryl conjugated carbanion intermediates. With this new approach, a variety of gem ‐diaryl compounds bearing acyclic all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters were synthesized in high yields and excellent enantioselectivities.

title: Carbonyl‐Rich Polyimide Covalent Organic Frameworks as Anode Coating for Uniform Sodium Deposition
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), by virtue of their structural diversity, high specific surface area, and facile functionalization, have emerged as a promising anode coating for sodium metal batteries (SMBs). Herein, we report two polyimide COFs (TATT‐NTCDA‑COF and TATT‐PMDA‑COF) constructed from isocyanurate‐based amine building blocks, which feature profuse ion‐binding active sites and a robust, ordered framework, thereby significantly enhancing ion transport, fostering uniform sodium deposition, and suppressing dendrite growth. Benefiting from this unique design and its reliable stability, the symmetric cell based on TATT‐NTCDA‑COF operates stably for over 1200 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When assembled into a full cell with a commercial Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) cathode, it delivers an initial discharge capacity of 107.4 mAh g −1 , retains 9.3% capacity after 800 cycles at 1 C, and maintains over 90% capacity retention even after 1390 cycles at 5 C and 750 cycles at 10 C. Thus, the rational design of carbonyl‐rich 2D COFs is of great significance for the construction of artificial anode coatings for SMBs.

title: Suprasilica Nanosieves for Selective Capture of Aromatics Over Cyclic Aliphatics in Hydrocarbon Feedstocks
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating aromatic from cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons remains a major challenge, as conventional distillation is both energy‐intensive and poorly selective. Here, we report supramolecular silica nanosieves (suprasilica) that integrate organic molecular recognition sites directly into robust inorganic matrices. A hexasila‐ureido‐trianglamine (Δ‐Si 6 ) is co‐condensed within the silica matrix through a self‐assembly sol–gel approach at controlled loadings to produce suprasilica sieves ( Δ‐SiN x ). In vapor sorption, Δ‐SiN x reject cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons while displaying high aromatic uptake, achieving benchmark ideal selectivity for benzene over cyclohexane (23.5, uptake 9.4 mmol g − 1 ) on Δ‐SiN20 and for toluene over methylcyclohexane (6.3, uptake 6.3 mmol g − 1 ) on Δ‐SiN10 . The selectivity was further confirmed by Dynamic Column Breakthrough experiments, which demonstrated efficient separation under dynamic conditions. Importantly, the Δ‐SiN x retain their molecular discrimination in the binary liquid phase, showing strong preferential uptake while preserving aromatic selectivity in neat naphtha and in diluted crude oil. Metadynamics simulations indicate that the selectivity is kinetic in origin, benzene passing the macrocyclic apertures with a modest barrier while cyclohexane is excluded. These suprasilica nanosieves deliver benchmark separation performance and provide a scalable, energy‐efficient strategy for hydrocarbon purification.

title: Anchored Fluoro‐Shielded Solvation for Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)‐based polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for solid‐state lithium metal batteries owing to their favorable overall electrochemical properties. However, conventional PVDF‐based polymer electrolytes suffer from uneven solvation distribution, discontinuous ion‐transport pathways, and unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces caused by residual solvents and porous PVDF frameworks. Herein, we report an anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation strategy to construct a high‐performance PVDF‐based polymer electrolyte. By integrating polyanionic anchoring sites with fluorinated shielding segments, the optimized electrolyte enables spatially distributed anion‐rich solvation pathways, homogeneous Li + transport, and robust LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The polymer electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.26×10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.69, an oxidative onset potential of 5.27 V, and a critical current density of 6.4 mA cm −2 . Spectroscopic and interfacial analyses reveal that the anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation structure promotes LiF‐rich SEI formation and suppresses solvent decomposition. Consequently, Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 batteries retain 80.2% capacity after 2000 cycles under high‐voltage and high‐rate conditions of 4.5 V and 5 C. This work highlights anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation as an effective molecular design principle for advanced polymer electrolytes toward practical high‐voltage and high‐rate solid‐state Li metal batteries.

title: Light‐Induced Ce–Ov–Ni Motifs Enable Hydrogen‐Poisoning‐Resistant Photothermal NH 3 Decomposition
abstract: ABSTRACT NH 3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H 2 release is hindered by N–H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle‐supported CeO 2 (Ni/CeO 2 ) for low‐temperature photothermal NH 3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO 2 , which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce–Ov–Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH 3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen‐vacancy‐associated sites favor NH 3 adsorption, N–H bond activation, and N‐containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy‐induced electronic modulation weakens H 2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H 2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N‐ and H‐containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO 2 achieves 96.3% NH 3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat −1 ·h −1 . It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat −1 ·min −1 H 2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light‐induced oxygen‐vacancy–metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen‐poisoning‐resistant NH 3 ‐to‐H 2 conversion.

title: Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy‐Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium‐Metal and Sodium–Ion Pouch Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐metal batteries are promising for low‐temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade‐off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME‐rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na + and anions (PF 6 − /BF 4 − ), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE‐rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic‐rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na + migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled‐up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.

title: Versatile Acetyl‐Functionalized Phenothiazine Self‐Assembled Monolayers for Efficient Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of versatile, stable, and cost‐effective hole‐transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next‐generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo‐PTZ (PTZ‐diBr), and diacetyl‐PTZ (PTZ‐diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ‐diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb 2 + ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built‐in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ‐diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ‐diACE achieve a power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS‐D‐2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ‐diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine‐based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.

title: Zwitterionic Thermoplastic Polyurethane‐Based Quasi‐Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries With Machine‐Learning‐Assisted Mechanistic Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a quasi‐solid‐state electrolyte based on zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane (QS‐Z‐TPU) for lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional quasi‐solid polymer electrolytes that mainly serve as passive liquid‐electrolyte reservoirs, QS‐Z‐TPU is designed as an active ion‐regulating matrix via phosphorylcholine‐derived zwitterionic groups in the TPU framework. The resulting electrolyte combines the elasticity and film‐forming capability of TPU with dual‐site ion regulation, where phosphate sites coordinate Li + while quaternary ammonium and urethane N‐H groups immobilize TFSI − anions. This design enhances electrolyte affinity while suppressing destructive swelling due to ionic crosslinking. QS‐Z‐TPU exhibits high ionic conductivity, a wide electrochemical stability window, and an enhanced Li + transference number. Machine‐learning‐assisted molecular modeling further reveals that the zwitterionic oligomer stabilizes separated LiTFSI configurations through cooperative Li + coordination and TFSI − association, substantially reducing the energetic penalty for ion‐pair separation. This regulated ion environment promotes uniform Li + flux at the lithium metal interface and facilitates the formation of a stable inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, QS‐Z‐TPU enables stable Li plating/stripping and improves the cycling stability and rate capability of LFP|Li full cells, further validated in flexible pouch‐cell demonstrations. These findings highlight zwitterionic molecular engineering as an effective strategy for interface‐stabilizing quasi‐solid electrolytes.

title: Decoupled Dual‐Stream Seawater Electrolysis Toward Cost‐Effective Green Hydrogen Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean, as a vast natural reservoir of ionic minerals, provides a promising approach to offset the high cost of hydrogen production from electrocatalytic water splitting. However, the complex ionic environment of seawater compels us to separate out scaling‐prone ions via cost‐effective membrane separation technology, and further separately electrolyze diluted and concentrated seawater to produce H 2 and high value‐added marine chemical products. We herein apply electrodialysis to separate out divalent cations and produce twofold concentrated seawater and fresh seawater. A decoupled dual‐stream seawater electrolysis (DDSE) strategy is designed. The fresh seawater is routed into an alkaline/AEM water electrolyzer to sustain stable H 2 evolution. The concentrated seawater is fed into a home‐made electrolyzer to produce NaClO and high‐purity Mg(OH) 2 . A scalable non‐noble metal‐based electrode (50 cm × 50 cm) was designed and fabricated with high activity and stability when applied in the chlorine evolution reaction. System‐level evaluation validates the feasibility of the DDSE strategy. Through rigorous techno‐economic analysis, the unit price of H 2 production is reduced to $0.39 kgH 2 −1 (DOE 2030 target: $1 kgH 2 −1 ), and the Global Warming Potential can be reduced up to 6.83%. This proposed DDSE strategy offers a new approach for cost‐effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.

title: Surpassing Metal‐Centric E‐Waste Recycling: Unveiling Graphite in Spent Lithium‐Ion Batteries Towards Electrocatalytic Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. The study revealed an interesting pattern, wherein the graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws by delivering an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Defects, surface activation, structural variation, and metal‐graphite synergism arising from prolonged cycle life served as a serendipitous finding of upcycling BM for OER, despite being loaded with impurities and/or degradation byproducts. Further, among these BM sets, direct upcycling of select graphite‐containing BM via mechanochemical functionalisation aided downsized derivatives delivering an overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , while functionalized graphite via bioleaching BM recorded an overpotential of 249 mV, an epoch‐making record in graphite upcycling. By correlating the overall insights using advanced material, electrochemical characterisation studies, and life cycle analysis, the current study unlocks spent graphite benefits for achieving sustainable energy solutions and beyond.

title: N‐Heterocyclic Molecular Additives Enable Solvation and Interfacial Chemistry Regulation for High‐Stability, High‐Rate, and High‐Capacity Lithium Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Most electrolyte additives enable long‐term Li plating/stripping at − 2 , non‐applicable to practical Li‐metal batteries (LMBs) operating at ≥5 mA cm − 2 and ≥ 5 mAh cm − 2 . Here, we report an interaction chemistry that enables simultaneous solvation and interfacial regulation by exploring a novel N‐heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC)—comprising an N‐heterocyclic core and four pyridine units–as an efficient additive for achieving ultra‐stable Li‐metal anodes under practical conditions. Electron‐rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion‐dipole interaction sites, inducing competitive coordination that weakens Li + solvation and enhances Li + migration in the bulk electrolyte, which homogenizes Li + concentration near the interface, favoring high‐rate Li deposition. TPTC also adsorbs on Li surface to construct a protective layer with a low interfacial de‐solvation barrier, which–together with low‐barrier Li + transport through heterocyclic cavities–facilitates uniform Li deposition. Meanwhile, electron‐deficient C–H sites in pyridine weakly interact with TFSI − , forming an anion‐rich interfacial region that in situ decomposes into an inorganic‐rich interphase, affording high‐flux Li + transport. This synergy allows stable Li plating/stripping at 10 mA cm −2 /10 mAh cm −2 for 3000 h. Paired with a high‐loading LiFePO 4 cathode (∼15 mg cm −2 ) and thin Li (∼100 µm), the cell maintains 87.8% capacity after 400 cycles.

title: A Retinal Matrix Stiffening Model Reveals FAK‐Dependent Mechanotransduction in Pericytes Underlies Vascular Destabilization
abstract: ABSTRACT Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC‐derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte‐endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human‐relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2 Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3 , HEY1 , JAG1 , and N‐cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)‐dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single‐cell RNA‐sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal‐adhesion components and alterations in Notch‐pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte‐mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.

title: Sub‐10 nm Confined Channels in Edge‐Closed MXene Nanoribbons Boost Proton Transport for Efficient Single‐Atom Electrocatalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoribbons from atomic layers such as graphene, carbides, and nitrides (MXenes) have attracted considerable interest owing to their distinct quantum confinement effects and high surface activity. However, the controlled synthesis of MXene nanoribbons remains challenging due to their random fragmentation and poor stability. Here, an efficient stiffness‐mediated strategy is developed to fabricate unique edge‐closed MXene nanoribbons, featuring a large aspect ratio of 10∼40 and confined channels of sub‐10 nm at both edges. The key protocol involves modulating the critical collapse pressure by reducing the bending stiffness of MXene layers, thereby triggering the tube collapse of pre‐formed nanoscrolls into edge‐closed nanoribbons upon solvent evaporation. The resulting nanoribbons exhibit an enhanced polarization electric field, leading to a higher surface proton concentration and enhanced proton transport rate compared to nanoscrolls and nanosheets. As a result, these MXene nanoribbons provide an efficient platform for anchoring single‐atom Pt, achieving a low overpotential of 23 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and a Tafel slope of 25 mV dec −1 in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), outperforming the most reported electrocatalysts.

title: Attribution Fingerprinting by Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Category‐Specific Additive Design Rules for Zinc Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are one of the most direct remedy for interfacial instability in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, yet their development remains empirical. Existing machine‐learning (ML) screening strategies presume a single global structure‐property relationship shared by all additives. Here, an interpretable ML framework predicts cycle life from molecular descriptors and test conditions, and molecule‐specific SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) profiles serve as attribution fingerprints. Unsupervised clustering resolves the additives into three attribution‐based categories, governed respectively by adsorption energetics, charge‐transfer gap and hydrogen‐bond‐network regulation, indicating that one universal descriptor set may not hold across chemically distinct additives. Representative additives from each category, none present in the training set, agree with experiment to within 11%. Category I screening identifies 2‐fluoropyridine‐5‐carbaldehyde (2FPD), predicted at 3218 h, and Zn//Zn cells deliver 3010 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 , within 6.5% of prediction. Structural controls trace the improvement to the aldehyde: retaining it alone gives 900 h against an 89 h baseline, whereas fluorine alone gives 90 h. 2FPD constructs a graded organic‐inorganic interphase that limits water access to the zinc surface and accelerates Zn 2+ desolvation, and Zn//MnO 2 full cells retain 96% capacity over 4000 cycles. This workflow offers a route towards interpretability‐guided additive design.

title: Quasi‐Continuous Multimodal Sensing of Urinary Oxalate Dynamics for Home‐Based Metabolic Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous at‐home monitoring of urinary oxalate dynamics is vital for the comprehensive management of hyperoxaluria and thus reduces the risk of kidney stone formation. However, home‐based devices for capturing dynamic oxalate profiles remain elusive, as urine is challenging to sample and unstable for subsequent biochemical testing. Here we report a remote multimodal sensing platform for achieving such urine monitoring during daily sequential urination through seamless embedding into a standard urine collection bucket. This platform integrates electrochemical oxalate sensing with simultaneous pH and urine‐volume measurements to correct the matrix drift in oxalate quantification. We achieve quasi‐continuous monitoring of 24 h urinary physicochemical dynamics under diet‐induced transient hyperoxaluria. By decoupling oxalate concentration from multimodal signals per urination, we reveal distinct metabolic response profiles under different dietary oxalate loads, providing new real‐time insights into oxalate metabolism and its associated risk of kidney stones. Our all‐in‐one sampling‐and‐testing platform could revolutionize clinical urine analysis for hyperoxaluria, shifting from a one‐time, multi‐day turnaround assay into a paradigm of quasi‐continuous monitoring with immediate feedback. This work represents a practical route toward personalized management of hyperoxaluria and a decentralized metabolic monitoring strategy for urology.

title: Cross‐System Recycling of Spent Layered Oxides Boosts Synergistic Optimization of Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 Cathodes via Site‐Selective Ni/Mn Co‐Doping
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the economic inviability of recycling spent sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) and the intrinsic drawbacks of Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) cathodes, a “cross‐system recycling” strategy is proposed to transform the waste layered oxides cathodes (NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 , NFM) into high‐performance polyanionic cathodes (Na 4 Fe 2.9 Ni 0.05 Mn 0.05 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 , NFNMPP). Nickel and manganese in the waste NFM that degrades due to “sodium deficiency” and irreversible phase transitions are leached out and doped into the NFNMPP lattice. Benefiting from the synergistic optimization of NFNMPP via site‐selective Ni/Mn co‐doping, the impurities and [P 2 O 7 ] distortion are suppressed, while the conductivity and Na + diffusion kinetics are enhanced. Consequently, the high‐purity NFNMPP (91.2%) exhibits an ideal initial coulombic efficiency of 92.84%, remarkable rate capability (75.21 mAh g −1 at 50 C), and excellent cycling stability (86.74% capacity retention after 12 000 cycles at 20 C). Furthermore, paired with hard carbon (HC) anode, NFNMPP//HC pouch cells exhibit high safety, a record‐long cycling life of 5557 cycles, 82.37% capacity retention at 30 C, and a wide operating temperature range (−40°C to 55°C), demonstrating great potential for energy storage applications and powering low‐speed electric vehicles. This study presents a viable pathway for optimizing cathode materials by recycling spent SIBs, and facilitates its practical applications validated by Ah‐level pouch cells.

title: High‐Mobility p‐Type Te x Se 1‐ x Films With Yb‐Enabled Oxidation Suppression for Short‐Wave Infrared Imaging Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Scalable high‐mobility p‐type semiconductor films hold considerable promise for advancing the performance of both photoelectronic devices and complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor technologies. Currently, tellurium (Te)‐based semiconductors exhibit high intrinsic hole mobility and compatibility with low‐temperature processing, making them promising candidates for cost‐effective p‐type materials. However, owing to their low Gibbs free energy, they are prone to oxidation into TeO 2 , which introduces deep‐level defects and severely degrades hole transport, thereby hindering practical applications. Here, we present an effective antioxidant strategy based on ytterbium (Yb) doping, wherein the strong Te–Yb bonding and high oxygen affinity of Yb effectively suppress the oxidation of Te to TeO 2 , fundamentally stabilizing Te x Se 1‐ x alloys. The resulting Te 0.7 Se 0.3 :Yb films exhibit a remarkable hole mobility of 177.5 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Furthermore, ZnO/Te 0.7 Se 0.3 :Yb photodetectors achieve a high responsivity of 0.21 A/W at 1300 nm, enabling multispectral imaging for precise target discrimination. These results demonstrate the Yb‐enabled oxidation suppression for Te‐based semiconductor, making a crucial stride toward the establishment of commercially viable high‐mobility p‐type semiconductor technology and short‐wavelength infrared photoelectronics.

title: Homojunction Back Contacts Enable Efficient Cu 2 O Photocathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing carrier separation and extraction is crucial to achieve efficient metal oxide photoelectrodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Here, we report a highly efficient Cu 2 O photocathode based on p + /p back‐contact homojunction. The homojunction significantly enhances hole‐selective extraction while suppressing electron backflow at the back‐contact interface, leading to marked improvements in PEC performance. The optimized photocathode delivers a hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) onset potential of 1.1 V and a saturated photocurrent density of ∼8.0 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the p + /p back homojunction design enables the fabrication of a semi‐transparent Cu 2 O photocathode, which, when integrated with a perovskite solar cell in a tandem configuration, achieves a solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 7.31%. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for advancing metal oxide photoelectrodes via homojunction engineering.

title: Dichlorobenzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione Derived Polymer Donor Enables Efficient Thin‐Film/Thick‐Film Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer donors with electron‐withdrawing benzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione (BDD) unit play an important role in improving power‐conversion‐efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs), although these achievements rely on high‐cost electron‐donating fluorinated thienyl‐benzodithiophene (BDTT) moiety. Herein, a dichlorobenzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione (BDD2Cl) unit is developed to design fluorine‐free BDTT‐ alt ‐BDD2Cl‐structured cost‐effective polymer donor (PBDTT‐BDD2Cl). Compared to its halogen‐free BDTT‐ alt ‐BDD‐structured control (PBDB‐T), PBDTT‐BDD2Cl shows deep‐shifted energy levels, improved solubility, crystallinity, and packing, tending to suppress energy loss, manipulate film‐forming kinetics, and improve charge transport properties. Accordingly, the PBDTT‐BDD2Cl:L8‐BO device demonstrates dramatically higher photovoltage (0.947 V) and lower non‐radiative energy loss (0.182 eV) and compared to the PBDB‐T:L8‐BO device (0.735 and 0.369 eV), while it achieves decreased PCE. When incorporating it into D18:L8‐BO host, ternary D18:PBDTT‐BDD2Cl:L8‐BO shows optimized donor/acceptor miscibility, delayed material nucleation, and prolonged molecular ordered packing duration, leading to boosted charge dynamics and favorable morphology. Thereby, thin‐film (100 nm) OSC achieves a superior PCE (21.1%, certified as 20.6%, ranking among the highest values) than the D18:PBDB‐T:L8‐BO control (19.3%), while its thick‐film (500 nm) device also obtains a top‐high PCE (17.3%) among these reported thick‐films (≥500 nm). This work highlights that BDD2Cl is an ideal candidate for developing cost‐effective polymer donors toward efficient thin‐film/thick‐film OSCs.

title: Selective Hydrogen Transport Through Polymeric Fullerene Nanosheet Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lamellar membranes, assembled from two‐dimensional (2D) nanosheets, have attracted intensive attention for molecular and ion sieving due to their tunable interlayer channels and ultrathin selective layers. However, molecular transport in conventional lamellar membranes usually occurs through interlayer galleries whose dimensions vary with stacking, limiting ångström‐scale control over selectivity. Therefore, developing a novel lamellar membrane with ångström‐scale in‐plane pores is highly desirable. In an idealized qTP lattice, four‐directionally connected fullerene cages define periodically distributed apertures that converge from an approximately 5.87 Å entrance to a 3.11 Å waist. Upon assembly, the constriction regions can discriminate by size, while their converging entrances and the intersheet galleries govern molecular access and transport resistance through the in‐plane apertures. The resulting polymeric fullerene nanosheet membrane exhibits an H 2 permeance of 3896 ± 107 GPU and an H 2 /CO 2 separation factor of 88.5 ± 5.9 for the separation of an equimolar H 2 /CO 2 mixture at 303.15 K and a total feed pressure of 100 kPa. The separation performance remains stable over 200 h of operation. This study establishes topology‐encoded pore geometry as a design principle for integrating short selective pathways with ångström‐scale molecular discrimination in lamellar membranes.

title: Thermodynamic stabilization of substrate protein within the GroEL:ES chaperonin cage
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-regulated GroEL/ES chaperonin of
                    Escherichia coli
                    promotes protein folding by transiently encapsulating unfolded substrate protein in a nano-cage formed by the cylindrical GroEL and the lid-shaped GroES. How this confinement modulates the folding energy landscape, allowing accelerated protein folding unimpaired by aggregation, remains incompletely understood. Prompted by recent observations suggesting that the chaperonin cavity may favor unfolding [I. Korobko
                    et al.
                    ,
                    Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A.
                    119
                    , e2213170119 (2022)], here we reinvestigated the effect of encapsulation on protein thermodynamic stability. To allow thermal unfolding of an encapsulated substrate protein, we generated a destabilized variant of maltose-binding protein (MBP) by introducing four mutations, quadruple mutant-MBP (QM-MBP), lowering the melting temperature (
                    
                      T
                      m
                    
                    ) from 63.6 °C to 44.3 °C. GroEL/ES accelerated the slow spontaneous folding of QM-MBP ~20-fold. The protein reached a native-like structure while encapsulated inside GroEL:ES, as demonstrated using hydrogen/deuterium exchange and single molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer analyses in presence and absence of the ligand maltose. Importantly, confinement in the thermally stable chaperonin shifted the cooperative unfolding transition of QM-MBP to a
                    
                      T
                      m
                    
                    of 52.4 °C, corresponding to a stabilization by 4.6 kcal mol
                    −1
                    . In-cage thermal unfolding was reversible, indicating that the environment of the chaperonin cavity is conducive to folding. These findings suggest that a thermodynamically stabilizing effect of the GroEL:ES cage contributes to promoting protein folding.

title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA–peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.

title: Rising cell-free DNA level tracks cancer-associated methylation signal and improves multicancer detection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cancer patients carry more circulating cell-free DNA (ccfDNA)—small DNA fragments shed into the blood—than healthy people. Most of this excess comes not from the tumor itself but from immune cells, suggesting that it would simply dilute the much smaller amount of tumor-derived DNA in a blood sample. Using a study of 1,480 previously untreated participants across 43 hospitals—including patients with 14 cancer types spanning all stages, patients with benign growths, and healthy volunteers—we show the opposite: as total ccfDNA rises, it becomes enriched, not diluted, in fragments carrying cancer-associated DNA methylation signatures, independent of cancer type, disease stage, and a broad panel of demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. In fact, total ccfDNA explains more variance in cancer-associated methylation signal than the disease stage itself. This basic biological finding suggests a coupling between immune cell activity and tumor methylation. It also has a practical implication: we show that rising ccfDNA concentration is associated with higher cancer detection sensitivity, even within disease stages and particularly in early-stage disease—stage I sensitivity varied from 0.55 in the lowest ccfDNA concentration tertile to 0.85 in the highest, and stage II from 0.59 to 0.86. This suggests that ccfDNA concentration should be considered as a stage-independent stratification variable for benchmarking cancer-detection tests. Interestingly, similar behavior was observed in patients with symptomatic benign lesions, suggesting a broader biological response to abnormal tissue growth and not something unique to malignancy.

title: Geochemical signatures of magnetite are conserved in diverse populations of environmental magnetotactic bacteria
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) synthesize intracellular magnetite nanoparticles in a genetically controlled manner. They may represent some of the earliest biomineralizing organisms on Earth, and a unique window into ancient life and the environments that hosted it. Yet, identification of their mineralogical remains in ancient rocks is highly challenging due to the lack of reliable and lasting proxies. Previous results obtained from laboratory cultures of single strains of MTB revealed trace element and Fe isotope patterns that are not shared by any other source of magnetite, which could be used as reliable proxies for the identification of ancient MTB. However, the environmental relevance of these previous findings for environmental and mixed population of MTB is unknown. We report the trace element and Fe isotope compositions of magnetite extracted from environmental MTB collected in the water column of Lake Pavin, France, and show that the most distinctive geochemical traits (enrichment in Mo, Se, Sn, and light Fe isotopes) of magnetite produced by MTB cultivated in the laboratory are conserved in environmental populations. They represent potential biological signatures that can be searched in ancient rocks and coupled with magnetic and mineralogical tracers to support the presence of MTB and reconstruct their emergence and evolution.

title: Core effectors of the Fusarium pan-effectome contribute to host specificity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Fusarium
                    fungi cause economically important diseases of cereal crops, including
                    Fusarium
                    head blight, ear blight, and root rot. Central to these interactions are secreted effector proteins that manipulate host biology to promote infection. In turn, plants have evolved to recognize effector activity to activate immune responses and restrict disease. Despite their importance, the diversity, conservation, and evolution of
                    Fusarium
                    effectors remain poorly understood. Here, we present the
                    Fusarium sambucinum
                    Species complex Effector Compendium (FUSEC), a sequence-defined pan-effectome constructed from 188 high-quality genomes representing 27 species. FUSEC comprises 4,057 sequence-defined effector families, including a conserved soft-core repertoire of 235 families present in at least 95% of isolates. Structure-guided comparisons reorganized these conserved families into 184 structure-defined groups, revealing relationships that extend beyond sequence similarity and identifying similarities to numerous experimentally characterized fungal (a)virulence factors. Despite their broad conservation, soft-core families exhibited substantial within-family sequence diversity, and analyses of diversifying selection identified 44 candidate families undergoing adaptive evolution. Functional screening revealed that the majority of these candidates altered wheat immune responses, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene deletions in
                    Fusarium graminearum
                    demonstrated that multiple conserved effectors contribute to cultivar-dependent
                    Fusarium
                    head blight severity.

title: Coupled outward and inward oxide growth during metal oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Metal oxidation is traditionally described as a dichotomy: oxide scales grow either outward via cation diffusion or inward via anion diffusion, with the dominant pathway determined by the prevailing point defects in the oxide lattice. Here, we demonstrate that these two modes are not mutually exclusive but intrinsically coupled within a single oxidation process. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy to monitor the oxidation of copper—a canonical cationic system—we directly visualize simultaneous oxide propagation at both the O
                    2
                    /Cu
                    2
                    O surface interface and the buried Cu
                    2
                    O/Cu interface. Complementary simulations reveal the mechanistic origin of this behavior. Outward cation transport during surface oxide growth injects a sustained flux of vacancies into the underlying metal lattice, which facilitates inward oxygen incorporation and drives oxide growth at the buried interface. This vacancy-mediated feedback couples cationic and anionic transport process, providing a unified framework in which surface cationic growth directly enables inward anionic-driven growth. By identifying vacancy injection as a key mediator of interfacial mass transport, this work provides a mechanistic basis for predicting oxidation kinetics and defect-regulated solid-state transformation pathways in reactive environments.

title: Unpacking transatlantic income inequality
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: This paper uses newly harmonized survey and register data on incomes and labor market outcomes as the basis for consistent comparisons of inequalities across 17 North American and European countries over the period 1995–2021. We examine trends in disposable income inequality in the working-age population, defined as persons aged 25 to 60, as well as its component parts of market income inequality and redistribution through government tax and transfer systems. We adjust incomes to allow for changes in education, population aging, and household structure in each country. We test for convergence across countries in demographically-adjusted disposable income inequality, along with market income inequality and redistribution. There is strong evidence of convergence over time in disposable income inequality across the 17 countries, despite a divergence in the dispersion of market income inequality driven by very heterogeneous trends for hours of work and the number of workers in households across countries. Consistent with this we find a strong convergence across countries in the dispersion of our measure of redistribution. There are reductions over time in inequality-reducing redistribution in the Nordic countries and increases in some other European and North American countries, with the net effect being more similarity across countries, a lower average level of redistribution, and a higher average level of disposable income inequality. These trends are being driven by the bottom 95% of the income distribution. Our results are robust to a variety of alternative specifications including the measure of inequality, trimming of data outliers, and sample period.

title: Engineered T cell–agonist chimera for logic-gated STING activation and augmented cancer immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The efficacy of adoptive T cell therapy against solid tumors is markedly hindered by the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Here, we demonstrate that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation in tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) enhances the intratumoral infiltration and cytotoxicity of adoptive T cells. We next design a TAM-targeted nanoagonist and engineer a T cell
                    –
                    agonist chimera (SNTC) via covalent surface anchoring, to achieve synchronized biodistribution of STING agonist with adoptive T cells. The nanoagonist is locally released in tumor tissue in response to the elevated reduction potential on T cell surface, followed by intracellular glutathione-mediated restoration of STING agonist in TAM, thereby enabling AND logic-gated STING activation. SNTC not only reshapes tumor stroma and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment to augment adoptive T cell function but also enhances the antigen presentation ability of TAM to activate endogenous T cells. SNTC elicits robust antitumor efficacy in melanoma tumor-bearing mice, resulting in over 40% survival beyond 60 d. Moreover, combining tumor-infiltrating T lymphocyte (TIL)-based SNTC with immune checkpoint blockade therapy leads to sustained tumor regression in mouse model of orthotopic pancreatic tumor. Collectively, SNTC holds translational potential to optimize STING activation for adoptive T cell therapy of cancer.

title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17,
                    P
                    < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08,
                    P
                    < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13,
                    P
                    < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04,
                    P
                    = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.

title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus–pituitary–testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified
                    Synage
                    , a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that
                    Synage
                    expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted
                    Synage
                    _B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of
                    Synage
                    in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically,
                    Synage
                    interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8–KCHIP4 interaction.
                    Synage
                    loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (
                    I
                    A
                    ), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent
                    Synage
                    loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8–KCHIP4–Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify
                    Synage
                    as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.

title: Spontaneous gas film expansion at an oil–water interface
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Spontaneous interfacial separation of oil and water, by inserting a gas film between the two liquids, is thermodynamically unfavorable because the oil–water interface is replaced by oil–gas and water–gas interfaces with a higher combined interfacial energy. Here, we demonstrate that microstructural confinement enables this transition after bubble introduction through the coupling of wetting, capillarity, and gas transport. Spontaneous oil imbibition into a water-submerged micropillar array, together with local contact-line pinning, deforms the oil–water interface into a metastable meniscus and generates a local pressure deficit in the confined oil. This deficit, combined with the bubble’s interfacial configuration, lowers its air partial pressure and promotes dissolved-air uptake from the surrounding water. Geometric confinement, reduced oil pressure, and low oil–gas interfacial tension favor bubble lateral invasion of adjacent oil-filled cells over vertical extrusion. As the gas front advances, meniscus relaxation and oil redistribution promote further wetting, renewing the capillary conditions that support gas film propagation. We develop a coupled transport-capillarity framework that captures these morphological transitions and predicts a characteristic timescale for gas film evolution, determined by the interaction among geometry, capillarity, and gas-phase transport. Spatially varying the microstructure further controls the propagation pathway and morphology of the gas film. These findings show how favorable wetting can support an energetically costly interfacial transformation through a confinement-induced capillary pressure field, providing a general mechanism for gas-mediated separation in confined multiphase systems.

title: Rapid target engagement of KRAS G12C tricomplex inhibitor RO3903 overcomes resistance and drives durable tumor regression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The clinical durability of first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors is constrained by resistance mechanisms, primarily the rapid, receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK)-mediated reactivation of KRAS to its drug-insensitive, guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound (ON) state. Here, we perform a systematic comparative characterization of clinical and investigational KRAS G12C inhibitors, including Sotorasib, Adagrasib, Divarasib, and Elironrasib, and our structurally optimized tricomplex ON inhibitor, RO7783903 (RO3903). We demonstrate that the covalent tricomplex inhibitors RO3903 and Elironrasib effectively outpace dynamic nucleotide cycling, conferring resilience to potent RTK stimulation and overcoming the secondary KRAS mutations that drive clinical resistance to guanosine diphosphate (GDP)-bound (OFF) state inhibitors. Notably, RO3903 potently inhibits tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner across multiple preclinical models, including an orthotopic intracranial model. Furthermore, RO3903 exhibits synergistic efficacy when combined with inhibitors targeting OFF-state KRAS G12C, YAP-TEAD, EGFR/MET, or FAK, as well as with anti-PD1 antibody and anti-PD1/VEGF bispecific antibody immunotherapies. The high potency, fast target engagement, and brain tumor inhibition of RO3903 position this molecule as a valuable tool reagent and a promising partner for combination strategies to achieve durable tumor regression.

title: How 20th-century immigrants did not have to change their last names in order to become American
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Reports of parents’ names in Social Security Application records allow us to quantify at a population level the extent and nature of historical last name changes by immigrants. Our analysis of European, Middle Eastern, and Asian immigrants of the early to mid-20th-century finds that more than 80% kept their last names. Computational linguistic analysis shows that most of those who did change preserved their surname’s ethnic signal, leaving only about 5% of all immigrants trying to disguise their foreign origins. Of these, Jewish immigrants had the highest rate of ethnicity-concealing last name changes; Italian, Japanese, and Chinese immigrants all had the lowest. Our proposed framework helps understand the variation: name changes were rarest where ethnic community networks were densest and where passing as unmarked was least credible—as among visibly non-White immigrants. Our findings challenge the dominant assimilationist narrative that immigrants in this era had to shed their foreign identities to enter the American mainstream. “Becoming White” by adopting an English surname was not a large part of historical immigrant experience. Rather, the overwhelming majority of immigrants chose to openly preserve their ethnic origins. Our results also suggest that nominal record linkage of historical immigrant populations may be more feasible than previously assumed.

title: Hepatocyte-derived exosomal miR-122 mediates liver-to-brain crosstalk and neuroinflammation in alcohol-exposed Alzheimer’s disease mice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Neuroinflammation and microglial activation are common features in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and excessive alcohol consumption. Alcohol induces liver damage and inflammation, and altered serum aminotransferases have been reported in patients with AD. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) and their cargo are emerging as mediators of intercellular communication in AD and alcohol-induced liver injury. However, the effects of alcohol use on AD progression remain to be elucidated. In this study, we evaluated the effects of repeated binge drinking on the liver and brain in the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD. Alcohol-exposed APP/PS1 mice showed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels, indicating liver injury absent in controls, along with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in both liver and brain. Alcohol increased the biogenesis and release of sEVs in AD mice and in mouse hepatocytes. These sEVs were enriched in mature miR-122-5p that is predominant in hepatocytes. In vivo, miR-122-5p was detected in the brain of alcohol-exposed AD mice suggesting EV-mediated miR-122-5p transfer to the brain. Microglial uptake of hepatocyte-derived sEVs was confirmed in vitro. sEVs from alcohol-treated hepatocytes sensitized BV-2 microglia to LPS stimulation, significantly enhancing CCL2, CXCL2, CCL3, and TNF-α production. Transfection of microglia with a miR-122-5p mimic partially recapitulated the pro-inflammatory sensitization by sEVs from alcohol-exposed hepatocytes, which was reversed by miR-122-5p inhibitor delivery. ADAM10, a miR-122-5p target, was reduced in both wild-type and AD brains after alcohol exposure, with cell-specific effects. These results suggest that alcohol-induced hepatocyte-derived sEVs may modulate liver-to-brain signaling via miR-122-5p and contribute to neuroinflammation in AD.

title: Senescent CD8 T effector memory cells are functionally impaired, enriched in aging and disease, and a barrier to immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Senescent cells play important roles in various biological processes that promote fitness and health; however, their timely elimination by immune cells is critical to maintain tissue homeostasis and prevent disease. Despite this, senescent cells accumulate systemically with age, suggesting that certain immune cells also become senescent and dysfunctional during aging. In support of this, we previously demonstrated that CD8 T cells, immune cells capable of targeting senescent cells, increasingly develop characteristics of senescence with advancing age in humans. Here, we characterized the senescence state of human SA-βGal-expressing (SA-βGal
                    high
                    ) CD8 T effector memory (EM) cells, their functional capabilities, and their enrichment in aging and disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T cells with unique transcriptional signatures develop in all stages of T cell differentiation, including in CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells, which increased in abundance with human aging. SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells expressed various classical markers of senescence and were significantly impaired in their ability to proliferate, produce cytokines, and eliminate senescent human stromal cells. Gene signatures of senescent SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells were enriched in CD8 T cells from older human donors, patients with age-related disorders, cancer, and in smokers. Furthermore, we show that T cell senescence is distinct from and dominant over T cell exhaustion, limiting the response of CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells to immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, our study demonstrates that senescence impairs CD8 T
                    EM
                    cell function and reveals the involvement of senescent and dysfunctional CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells in aging, disease, smoking, and responses to immunotherapy.

title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the “middle-of-the-road” SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. The updated forcing dataset used in the atmosphere model does not improve the agreement between the simulated global-mean top-of-the-atmosphere radiation trends and the satellite-observed trends. Regionally, we identify pronounced shifts in radiative energy partitioning between atmosphere and surface. Specifically, during 2001–2021, accelerated reductions in sulfate and black carbon aerosols over East Asia drive a significant decline in atmospheric solar absorption that matches observations, while a substantial increase in organic aerosols at higher latitudes induces a localized increase in atmospheric absorption that does not match observations. The substantial influence of localized forcing changes on simulated regional climate underscores the necessity for routine updates of forcing datasets.

title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host–microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. This study investigates the cospeciation and molecular adaptations of
                    Curvibacter
                    to its host
                    Hydra
                    , a well-established model for the study of host–microbe interactions. We provide strong evidence of cospeciation, as demonstrated by phylogenetic congruence between different
                    Hydra
                    species and their corresponding
                    Curvibacter
                    symbionts, along with preferential recolonization of germ-free
                    Hydra
                    by their native
                    Curvibacter
                    strains. Comparative genomic analyses reveal that host-associated
                    Curvibacter
                    strains exhibit distinct metabolic and biosynthetic adaptations compared to their free-living relatives. Specifically, the enrichment of proteins linked to host glycan interactions, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), DNA metabolic processes, ABC transport, sugar metabolism, and bacterial chemotaxis highlights specialized adaptations of

title: Subcellular compartment determines signal dominance: Endosomal cAMP overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation from a single receptor
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cells convey information not only via the identity of activated signaling pathways but also through the subcellular location where those signals originate. Whether spatially distinct signals from a single activated receptor compete to determine net cellular output has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate this principle for a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), showing that endosomal and plasma membrane signals from a single activated receptor are not merely distinct but functionally opposed, with endosomal signaling predominating to reverse the net cellular output. Using the adhesion GPCR GPR64/ADGRG2 as a model system, we show that ligand activation engages two spatially distinct G-protein pathways that are not just additive but functionally opposed: plasma membrane G
                    13
                    /RhoA activation and Gs/cAMP production that persists from endosomes following receptor internalization. The endosomal cAMP pool actively overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation, resulting in net RhoA inactivation, an outcome that is completely reversed by pharmacological blockade of endocytosis or endosomal G
                    s
                    inactivation. In parathyroid cells, where GPR64 is highly expressed, this endosomal signal dominance suppresses parathyroid hormone secretion independently of extracellular Ca
                    2+
                    levels. These findings support a model in which the subcellular compartment, rather than pathway identity, determines the dominant signal and the overall cellular response of a single activated receptor, with implications for understanding the complexity of GPCR signaling.

title: Dissociation of gravity and limb dynamics in motor control
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Human movements remain accurate across substantial variations in mechanical loading, yet how the nervous system anticipates and compensates for intrinsic and extrinsic forces when generating muscle commands remains unresolved. Because the forces acting on the body are complex and nonlinear, dynamical modeling provides a powerful framework for identifying the computations underlying motor control. Here, we exploited parabolic flight to dissociate gravitational loading from intrinsic limb dynamics and directly test how these mechanical components are represented in motor commands. We analyzed kinematics and shoulder muscle activity from nine participants performing visually guided pointing movements in microgravity (0g), normogravity (1g), and hypergravity (2g). Inverse dynamics revealed that the gravity-independent component of muscle torque remained invariant across gravitational conditions. In striking contrast, muscle moments estimated from muscle activation showed systematic scaling of not only static but also phasic components with gravitational load, particularly during movement deceleration. This divergence arises because activation-derived muscle moments capture cocontraction, and thus impedance-related control, that is absent from net torques obtained by inverse dynamics. Gravity-dependent regression analyses further showed that muscle activation could be reconstructed from a compact set of mechanical variables dominated by gravity-dependent torque and movement velocity, revealing a low-dimensional structure of motor control. Together, these findings support a control architecture in which motor commands integrate predictive compensation for limb dynamics with gravity-dependent regulation of muscle cocontraction. This dual strategy provides a mechanism for maintaining stable and accurate movement across changing mechanical environments and offers a unified framework for understanding motor control under variable external loads.

title: Lignin‐Based Supramolecular Dynamic Networks: A General Platform for Energy Harvesting and Sensing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lignin‐ based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio‐based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self‐healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.

title: Scalable Gigapascal Strength Bamboo Veneers via Nanocellulose Reinforcement
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon neutrality demands materials that deliver both performance and low environmental impact. Carbon fiber and glass fiber rely on fossil feedstocks and energy‐intensive processing, while nature bamboo the ecological marvel is limited by inefficient load transfer within their heterogeneous cell walls. Here we show that this limitation can be overcome by reprogramming the bamboo cell wall through supramolecular nano‐reinforcement. Cellulose nanocrystals infiltrate the cell wall and promote the reorganization of the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network within the aligned cellulose framework converting structural discontinuities into a continuous load‐bearing scaffold. This enhances interfibrillar stress transfer and homogenizes mechanical response across scales. The resulting material achieves a tensile strength of 0.98 GPa and a Young's modulus of 52.7 GPa, with specific strength rivaling many synthetic fiber materials. These gains are achieved with up to two orders of magnitude lower carbon intensity than that of carbon fiber. This work demonstrates a scalable route to transform abundant biomass into high‐performance structural materials, decoupling mechanical performance from carbon intensity.

title: PASS‐Derived O/S Donor Field‐Directed Competitive–Cooperative Fe/Co Phase Evolution for Cross‐Band Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Fe/Co bimetallic regulation enables high‐performance microwave absorbers, yet the role of intrinsic coordination disparity in precursor conversion, nonequilibrium phase evolution, and cross‐band loss redistribution remains unclear. We design a poly(arylene sulfide sulfone) (PASS)‐predefined O/S heterogeneous donor‐field strategy to direct competitive–cooperative nonequilibrium phase evolution in Fe/Co systems. Covalently embedded sulfone‐O and thioether‐S sites, with PASS's rigid backbone, create a molecularly preorganized donor field that amplifies non‐equivalent Fe/Co coordination, promoting competitive bonding, differentiated phase pathways, and electronic‐state reconstruction during confined pyrolysis. Fe/Co regulation thus reshapes local phases, O/S chemical environments, and interfacial charge states via Fe─O/Co─S coordination preferences, generating multiphase heterostructures, amorphous/crystalline interfaces, defects, and lattice strain while balancing dielectric polarization, conductive transport, magnetic response, and impedance matching. The resulting CFC absorber achieves cross‐band absorption in low‐frequency 5G and high‐frequency radar bands. CFC‐4 exhibits −73.83 dB at 6.23 GHz (3.20 mm) and −76.59 dB at 16.98 GHz (1.31 mm), with a maximum EAB of 5.03 GHz. CFC‐4∼6 (1–5 mm) show >90% cumulative effective absorption over 2–18 GHz. Finite‐element simulations reveal a maximum RCS reduction of 42.5 dB on PEC. This work establishes O/S donor‐field engineering as a viable route to amplify Fe/Co coordination differentiation for efficient cross‐band microwave absorption.

title: Sulfur Locking and Chlorination Synergistically Enable Efficient Charge Transport and Low Nonradiative Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient charge transport while maintaining low nonradiative energy loss remains a key challenge in the molecular design of small‐molecule acceptors (SMAs) for organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a stepwise molecular engineering strategy based on sulfur locking and chlorination to regulate intermolecular packing and excited‐state properties simultaneously. Sulfur locking modifies molecular conformation and intermolecular packing, leading to enhanced exciton diffusion and charge transport. Subsequent chlorination further strengthens intermolecular interactions through additional Cl···S contacts, resulting in tighter π–π stacking and improved crystalline ordering. Binary OSCs based on D18:Qx2Ph‐SCl achieve an efficiency of 20.0% with a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.951 V, while maintaining a low nonradiative energy loss of ∼0.19 eV. Owing to its intrinsically lower reorganization energy and weaker electron–phonon coupling than L8‐BO, Qx2Ph‐SCl further serves as an effective third component in ternary OSCs, reducing nonradiative recombination and increasing the V OC . As a result, the ternary device delivers an efficiency of 21.3%. This work demonstrates that stepwise sulfur locking and chlorination provide an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously optimizing charge transport and voltage loss in high‐performance OSCs.
