As a result, Mo 5 O 14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g −1 at 1.5 A g −1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g −1 even at 300 A g −1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg −1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg −1 , and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.

title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%‐Efficient DMF‐Based Kesterite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu 2 SnSe 3 ‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd 2+ partially substitutes Zn 2+ sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.

title: Structure‐Encoded Magnetic Anisotropy in Super‐Tough Magnetoelastic Aramid–Silk–Magnetite Fibers
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic anisotropy is essential for controlling magnetic responses in soft matter, yet it is conventionally imposed using external magnetic fields. Here, we show that magnetic anisotropy can instead be intrinsically encoded and continuously tuned through hierarchical structural organization, establishing a route by which anisotropic dipolar interactions, rather than conventional shape effects, dominate the magnetic energy landscape. This mechanism is achieved by engineering composite nanofibrils in which magnetite nanoparticles are grown in situ within an aligned aramid–silk matrix, inspired by biomineralization in chiton teeth. The resulting aramid–silk–magnetite fibers combine high strength and modulus with exceptional toughness up to 820 MJ m − 3 , while exhibiting tunable magnetic anisotropy spanning axial to radial easy‐axis configurations through structural relaxation. Quantitative analysis reveals that collective dipolar coupling dominates magnetic anisotropy by orders of magnitude over demagnetization‐field contributions, identifying nanoparticle interaction networks as the primary origin of anisotropy. This built‐in anisotropy enables strain‐mediated reconfiguration of magnetic properties, giving rise to magnetoelastic coupling that scales with fiber modulus and reflects the available structural mobility for magnetic reorientation. By amplifying structure‐defined anisotropy under mechanical loading, we further demonstrate strain‐controlled magnetic torque for actuation. These findings establish a structural design principle for programming magnetic anisotropy in mechanically robust magnetoelastic materials.

title: High‐Entropy Complementary d‐Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li 2 S in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single‐component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi‐step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high‐entropy complementary d‐band center model, extending the classical d‐band center theory to multi‐metal systems. The complementary d‐band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi‐metal sites collaboratively construct a “highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption” closed‐loop pathway, with the d‐p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high‐entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li‐S batteries.

title: In Situ Bulk Passivation and Carrier Transport Modulation in Te‐TeO x Films Enable Low‐Noise Monolithic Near‐Infrared Imagers
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR) imagers are essential for applications ranging from material sorting and autonomous driving to biomedical diagnostics, yet their performance is often limited by severe carrier recombination and high dark current. Here, we demonstrate a low‐noise NIR photodiode based on Te‐TeO x nanocrystalline‐in‐matrix films, in which the surrounding oxide matrix provides in situ bulk passivation and enables the modulation of carrier transport to balance carrier loss and extraction. This approach reduces trap density, suppresses recombination, and prolongs carrier lifetime, while controlled oxide incorporation tunes the optical bandgap and interfacial offsets of the heterojunction photodiode, resulting in spectral response spanning the visible and NIR regions with low dark current. The resulting photodiodes exhibit a low dark current of 9.70 nA cm −2 at a bias of −10 mV, a detectivity of 3.85 × 10 12 Jones and an ultralow detectable power of 1.35 pW for NIR photodetection. The strategy is compatible with direct monolithic integration with readout integrated circuits, enabling a 256 × 256 focal‐plane imager with excellent pixel uniformity. It further supports high‐quality focal‐plane imaging in both visible and NIR regions, as well as solution identification and imaging through smoke.

title: Ambipolar Fiber Amplifiers for Highly Sensitive Biosignal Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological signals are inherently weak and susceptible to noise, making in situ signal amplification critical for high‐fidelity sensing. Electronic fibers offer unique advantages for conformal and scalable biointegration; however, fiber amplifiers are seldom reported due to the lack of suitable semiconducting materials that combine balanced ambipolar transport, scalable fiber fabrication, and high device performance. Herein, we report the first single‐component ambipolar fiber platform based on a newly designed polymer, P(gTDPP‐TQ), which combines balanced p‐ and n‐type transport, low‐cost synthesis, and continuous fiber fabrication. Fiber processing enhances molecular ordering and charge transport, yielding record‐high µC * and g m,norm among reported semiconducting fibers, enabling high‐performance fiber amplifiers with a high voltage gain of up to 150 V V −1 and low operating voltages down to 0.5 V. These fiber amplifiers enable high‐fidelity electroencephalogram signal amplification over 20 times and sensitive cortisol sensing with a record‐low detection limit of 3.7 fM. This work establishes a general ambipolar fiber platform for integrated bioelectronic amplification and sensing.

title: A Noninvasive Approach to Study Localized Forces in 3D Epithelia
abstract: ABSTRACT Epithelial tissue integrity and remodeling rely on mechanical coupling between cytoskeletal organization and adhesion complexes, but their orchestration in three‐dimensional (3D) epithelia remains unresolved. Here, we introduced a noninvasive strategy to locally probe forces within 3D epithelial tissues. We engineered elastic polyacrylamide (PAAm) microbeads with cell‐like size and mechanical properties, enabling their integration into tissues. PAAm microbeads were spontaneously engulfed by the tissue, establishing an intrinsic interface. This allowed bead deformation to be directly correlated with local cytoskeletal architecture and adhesion organization, visualized through high‐resolution imaging and quantitative 3D computational reconstruction. Using this approach, we demonstrated that localized mechanical perturbations trigger cytoskeletal remodeling while preserving tissue polarity. We further identified extracellular matrix composition as a key determinant of bead‐tissue interactions. At the bead–cell interface, cells assembled tension‐bearing focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. Quantitative analysis of bead deformation revealed sub‐cellular scale patterns of cell‐bead interaction forces, which correlated with the localization of cytoskeletal elements. Our findings extend previous traction force microscopy observations to 3D, revealing coordinated, spatially heterogeneous forces specifically at the cell–bead interface. Taken together, this enabled us to dissect the interplay between cellular processes and tissue mechanics in a noninvasive way in 3D model systems.

title: Smart Luminescent Materials: From Basic Luminophores to Stimuli‐Responsive Luminescent Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Smart luminescent materials (SLMs) represent an emerging class of intelligent optical systems that can convert external stimuli into adaptive and programmable photonic outputs. By integrating molecular photophysics with dynamic structural regulation, SLMs enable precise modulation of emission intensity, wavelength, polarization, lifetime, and energy conversion pathways with high spatiotemporal controllability. Recent advances in molecular engineering, supramolecular assembly, and hierarchical material design have driven a transition from conventional luminescence switching toward multifunctional systems featuring multilevel, multistimulus, and information‐enriched optical responses. This review provides a comprehensive and mechanism‐oriented overview of recent progress in SLMs across diverse material platforms, including solution‐phase systems, solid‐state materials, dynamic hydrogels, chiral circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) systems, and lanthanide‐doped upconversion nanoparticles. Particular emphasis is placed on how external stimuli regulate excited‐state electronic structures, molecular conformations, supramolecular organizations, and hierarchical architectures to achieve adaptive luminescent behaviors. In addition, emerging strategies for stimuli‐responsive CPL regulation and intelligent photon conversion based on upconversion nanomaterials are highlighted, demonstrating how molecular‐level control can be translated into dynamic optical functionalities. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed toward the rational design of next‐generation smart luminescent materials for applications in information security, wearable electronics, soft robotics, biophotonics, and intelligent photonic devices.

title: Non‐Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (Na x Sn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the Na x Sn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na 2 O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF 2 ||Na x Sn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||Na x Sn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g −1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.

title: Coordination Bridges in Confined‐Water Domains Enable Partially Desolvated Zn 2 + Transport in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next‐generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. However, their commercialization is severely hindered by poor cycle stability, primarily originating from dendritic Zn growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution. To address these challenges simultaneously, we design and integrate a multifunctional polymeric protective layer incorporating amide and imidazolium functional groups. The zincophilic amide groups facilitate ion transport by providing stable Zn 2+ binding sites, whereas the hygroscopic imidazolium groups establish a confined‐water domain that regulates local solvation dynamics. Within this domain, water molecules transiently stabilize Zn 2+ and act as a coordination bridge during ion migration, yet their mobility toward the electrode surface is restricted. This dual functionality increases the Zn 2+ single‐ion conductivity 6.55‐fold and reduces the hydrogen evolution rate by 79.1%. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit markedly extended cycling lifetimes of up to 2200 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . When applied to Zn–I 2 full cells, the protective layer enables stable operation over 4000 cycles with >85% capacity retention, even under a practical areal capacity of 3.6 mAh cm −2 . These findings highlight a robust interfacial strategy to realize long‐duration, high‐capacity aqueous ZIBs for grid‐scale energy storage.

title: In Situ Probing of Small‐Molecule Electrolysis Using Ambient‐Pressure X‐Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic small‐molecule conversion addresses the need to couple renewable electricity with sustainable fuel and chemical production, yet challenges remain in resolving the dynamic gas/solid/liquid interfaces that govern catalytic activity, selectivity and stability. A key challenge is to correlate catalyst structures, reaction intermediates and local interfacial environments under comparable operating conditions. Ambient‐pressure x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provides surface‐sensitive and chemically specific information on catalyst chemical states, interfacial species and local electrostatic environments at the same working interface, enabling direct correlations between catalyst evolution and reaction intermediates. We offer a forward‐looking review of APXPS for probing gas/solid/liquid interfaces in small‐molecule electrolysis. We discuss three categories of electrochemical XPS/APXPS configurations: quasi‐in situ XPS, in which electrochemically treated catalysts are transferred under protected conditions for post‐reaction analysis; thin‐electrolyte‐film (dip‐and‐pull) APXPS, which probes a potential‐controlled interface through a nanometer‐scale liquid film; and membrane‐based APXPS, which accesses catalyst–ionomer–electrolyte interfaces. We introduce present‐day challenges in electrochemical APXPS and describe a vision towards more realistic operating conditions, higher time resolution and multimodal measurements integrated with theoretical and data‐driven spectral analysis. These developments provide potential avenues to establish reliable structure–intermediate–environment relationships in the further development of small‐molecule electrocatalysis.

title: Threshold‐Voltage Ion Sieving in Ultrathin Polymeric Membranes for Energy‐Efficient Lithium Extraction
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels achieve multi‐ion discrimination through parallel chemically distinct channel types, each optimized for a single ion species. Replicating this within a single synthetic membrane has remained beyond reach, for conventional membrane resistance blocks the bonding energy difference between different ions. Here we show that an ultrathin polymeric membrane (ca. 8.56 nm) bearing aligned angstrom‐scale porphyrin pores, fabricated by interfacial superspreading, reduces internal resistance sufficiently and achieves simultaneous multi‐ion discrimination. Under a microvolt‐scale applied voltage, the membrane separates six ion species across three valence groups. In particular, the membrane exhibits anomalous selectivity for Li + , with a threshold voltage V t ≈ 400 mV which is 370 mV above the nearest competitor. Applied to lithium extraction from low‐quality brines, a two‐stage device achieves >98% recovery at 1.1 × 10 −4 Wh g −1 (Li) , three orders of magnitude below conventional electrodialysis. This membrane architecture offers a broadly applicable design principle for energy‐intensive separations in which resolving ions of similar charge and size is the critical challenge.

title: Cross‐Scale Decoupling of Mechanics and Kinematics in Chiral Tensegrity Metamaterials
abstract: ABSTRACT Compression‐torsion metamaterials (CTMs) that break spatial inversion symmetry face persistent trade‐offs among large deformation capacity, intrinsic stiffness, and fatigue durability. Crucially, boundary rotation induced by axial compression complicates integration with rotationally constrained engineering interfaces. Here we introduce a chiral three‐rod tensegrity cell (CTTC) paradigm that addresses these conflicts through a cross‐scale dual‐decoupling strategy. First, mechanical decoupling at the unit‐cell scale separates macroscopic shape‐morphing from large local material strain: a heterogeneous rigid‐flexible architecture channels global compression into kinematic rod displacement and uniform elastic‐network stretching, achieving 97° torsion at Level 0 and only 4.87% peak‐force degradation over 10 000 cycles at Level 3. An integrated geometric interlocking reconfigurator further enables post‐fabrication programmability of stiffness and strain‐normalized twist ratio ( R T‐S ). Second, kinematic decoupling at the assembly scale localizes torsional deformation as a boundary‐decoupled internal rotational mode, while maintaining external interfaces in pure translation. This cross‐scale framework establishes a deployable paradigm bridging metamaterial physics and robotic systems operating in geometrically constrained environments.

title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space
abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 10 4 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of 9.7 − 2.7 + 3.2 pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

title: In the image of their tools
Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

title: Chiral Two-Dimensional Perovskite Single Crystals Enable Flexible Piezoelectric Nanogenerators for High-Sensitivity Ultrasound Detection
abstract: Abstract Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.

title: Novel Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors Based on Double Electron‐Deficient Central Core for High‐Performance Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid advances in A‐DA'D‐A fused‐ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non‐radiative energy loss (Δ E 3 ) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron‐deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT‐4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron‐deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4‐c:3′,4′‐g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross‐coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT‐4F exhibits extended π‐conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid‐state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed Δ E 3 in PM6:CBT‐4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced Δ E 3 , PM6:CBT‐4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT‐4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT‐4F as a high‐performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors.

title: Heterometallic Polarization Enabling Precise Intermediate Regulation for Selective CO 2 Photoreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO 2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO 2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 2.5 ) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g −1 h −1 —10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 0 )—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH 4 . MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 7.5 ) delivers a CH 4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g −1 h −1 —28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 0 ) and MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 2.5 ), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO 2 conversion.

title: A Multi‐Topologically Superposed Mechanically Interlocked Polymer
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi‐topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer ( MIP ) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na + transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi‐topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.

title: Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO 2 for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO 2 as a renewable one‐carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible‐light‐driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO 2 activation toward either one‐electron radical anion (CO 2 •– ) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface‐bound CO 2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO 2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β‐selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO 2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13 C‐labeled product and gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO 2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.

title: Spirobisindane‐Based Microporous Nanofilms With Tunable Network for Precise Molecular Sieving
abstract: ABSTRACT Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m 2 g −1 ) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 ), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH 2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH 2 and SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.

title: Hydroxyl‐Mediated Proton Transfer Over Cu Single Atoms Decorated TiO 2 for Selective Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction to Ethanol
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C 2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)‐rich TiO 2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO 2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C 2 H 5 OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g −1 h −1 with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C 2 H 5 OH at 361.5 µmol g −1 h −1 with 99.4% yield‐based selectivity, which is related to Cu 2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high‐performance and low‐cost photocatalyst for CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single‐atom–surface‐group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.

title: Electrochemical Indicators for Designing Durable Low‐Pt Fuel Cell Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)‐based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt‐based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m 2 g Pt −1 ) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.

title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

title: Record‐High Toroidal Blocking in a {Cu 6 Dy 3 } Single Molecular Toroid
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐molecule toroids (SMTs) are promising for quantum technologies because their vortex‐like spin arrangement generates magnetically silent ground states with minimal stray fields and enhanced protection against decoherence. However, their technological potential requires toroidal states that remain stable under strong external magnetic fields, since weak intramolecular interactions can induce spin flips and destroy toroidal order. In this study, we report heterometallic {3d–4f} complexes, [Ln 3 Cu 6 L 6 (µ 3 ‐OH) 6 (µ 1 ‐H 2 O) 6 ] 3+ (Ln = Dy ( 1 ), Y ( 2 ); L 2− = (S,E)‐ N ‐(2‐( λ 1 ‐oxidaneyl)‐1‐phenylethyl)‐1‐(3‐methoxy‐2‐( λ 1 ‐oxidaneyl)phenyl)ethan‐1‐imine)). Remarkably, the Dy(III) analogue retains its magnetically silent toroidal ground state up to 1.3 T, establishing an unprecedented benchmark for toroidal magnetization blocking and extending the field stability of molecular toroidal states beyond previous limits. Sub‐kelvin µ‐SQUID measurements, high‐frequency EPR spectroscopy, and theoretical modelling show that this high blocking field originates from an unexpectedly strong Dy–Dy exchange interaction, suggested to arise from neighboring Cu(II) ions, whereas direct ferromagnetic Cu–Dy exchange weakly destabilizes the toroidal state. These results reveal a new strategy for stabilizing toroidal states at high fields through targeted control of intramolecular exchange interactions, opening opportunities for electrically addressable molecular nanomagnets and quantum technologies.

title: Conjugation Interruption in 1D COFs for Boosted Charge Separation and Photocatalytic 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp 3 ) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.

title: Ultrastable NIR Absorbing Imidazole‐Based Open‐Shell Diradicaloids for High‐Efficiency Photothermal Steam and Power Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐shell diradicaloids are promising photothermal materials owing to their near‐infrared absorption and efficient non‐radiative energy dissipation. However, complex synthesis and inherent reactivity make them less relevant for practical applications. Herein, we report a stable, synthetically readily accessible pyrene‐integrated imidazole‐based open‐shell diradical ( PBQ ) photothermal material. PBQ possesses a high diradical character, with a low Δ E S‐T of −2.8 kcal/mol, and strong solid‐state absorption extending to ∼1600 nm. Under one‐sun illumination for 10 min, PBQ attains a surface temperature of 71°C and exhibits high photothermal solar steam generation of 2.05 kg m − 2 h − 1 with a solar‐to‐vapour conversion efficiency of 98%. Notably, PBQ outperforms previously reported diradicaloid‐based photothermal materials. PBQ exhibits excellent chemical‐ and photo‐stability even after 40 days of water soaking and 14 days under natural sunlight, or under high‐light intensity up to 2 suns for 120 mins. The high stability of PBQ is attributed to extensive delocalisation of the spin density across its large π‐conjugated backbone and the presence of stabilising heteroatoms. Additionally, PBQ exhibits photothermal power generation and simultaneous cogeneration of steam and electricity. This work demonstrates an imidazole‐linked diradicaloid as a high‐performance photothermal material, offering a molecular platform for solar‐driven water purification and energy conversion.

title: Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and 13 C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D 2 O as the Deuterium Source
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD 3 ) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD 3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D 2 O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD 3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD 3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13 CH 3 / 13 CD 3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD 3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K 2 CO 3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD 3 isotopic architectures.

title: Synergistically Modulating Electronic Structure and Interfacial Wettability of MnF 2 /NF−CNF Toward Enhanced Oxygen Reduction in Zinc−Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF 2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF 2 /NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF 2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half‐wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm −2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn‐based/heteroatom‐doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF 2 modulating p‐orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple‐phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm −2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.

title: Ionomer‐Free Iridium Anodes With Low Loading for Zero‐Gap Electrolyzers via Direct Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer‐free catalyst layers based on custom‐made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using as counter‐reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 . The PEMWE cell‐level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst‐coated membrane anode despite lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low‐loading ALD‐made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 . Plasma‐enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower‐activity . Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer‐bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.

title: ZrO 2 Clusters Enabling Room‐Temperature Hydrogen Absorption and Low‐Temperature Desorption of Commercial Mg Powder for Reversible Hydrogen Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium‐based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large‐scale utilization. Here, the amorphous‐carbon‐stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub‐2 nm ZrO 2 nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac) 4 ). The optimized Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr composite achieves rapid hydrogen absorption of 4.25 wt.% at 30°C within 60 min and exhibits high cycling stability with nearly no H 2 capacity fading after 40 cycles at 300°C under 30 bar H 2 . Notably, the Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr sample enables reversible hydrogenation at room temperature and dehydrogenation at high temperature, achieving better energy efficiency than conventional thermally driven MgH 2 and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO 2 /Mg interface accelerates H 2 adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.

title: Interface‐Confined Cationic Polarization Enables Rapid and Reversible Polyiodide Conversion for High‐Rate Zinc–Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries are promising for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their application is limited by sluggish polyiodide redox kinetics and severe shuttle effect. Many cathode‐regulation strategies improve iodine chemistry through physical confinement and polar adsorption. However, simultaneously suppressing polyiodide shuttling and enabling rapid iodine conversion remains challenging, particularly under high‐rate where fast interfacial redox kinetics are required. Here, interface‐confined cationic polarization is established by integrating π‐delocalized guanidinium cations (Gdm + ) into iodine cathodes, where cation–π interactions with Ketjen Black (KB) sp 2 carbon domains confine Gdm + on the KB surface. The delocalized positive charge of interface‐confined Gdm + electrostatically enriches polyiodides within the cathode, while its delocalized π‐electron system polarizes the electron cloud of iodine species and promotes interfacial charge transfer, enabling reversible polyiodide conversion without irreversible trapping. The optimized I 2 cathode delivers 100 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh‐rate of 50 A g −1 (∼237 C) and sustains 40 000 cycles with only 0.002% decay per cycle. A 1.0 Ah pouch cell retains 82.6% capacity after 1200 cycles. This work demonstrates interface‐confined cationic polarization as an effective strategy for regulating polyiodide redox chemistry, offering a new route toward high‐rate and long‐life Zn–I 2 batteries.

title: Cathode‐Driven Aluminothermic Fronts Amplify Thermal Runaway in Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal runaway in lithium‐ion batteries often develops from a local failure into a spatially propagating high‐temperature front. Here, we show that oxygen‐bearing cathode materials and metallic aluminium can form self‐sustained, glowing, cathode‐driven aluminothermic fronts in inert gas as a heat‐amplification pathway relevant to severe thermal runaway. Using a mesoscale platform based on semi‐1D composite bars, we isolate this interfacial redox chemistry from gas‐phase combustion, internal short‐circuit heating, and other coupled cell‐failure processes. Nickel‐rich layered oxide/aluminium bars sustain aluminothermic‐front propagation in argon, with velocities of the same order of magnitude as reported thermal‐runaway fronts. By varying aluminium loading, reaction atmosphere and cathode chemistry, we show that front propagation depends on aluminium fuel supply, the oxygen‐donor capability of the cathode, and access to oxygen gas. Crystalline phase and chemical‐state analyses reveal Li–Al–O/Al–O products together with reduced or reconstructed transition‐metal species, supporting cathode‐to‐aluminium oxygen transfer as the underlying redox pathway. For a representative 2‐Ah cell, energy‐audit calculations indicate that the aluminium‐cathode reaction gives a potential heat scale equivalent to about half of the stored electrical energy. These findings identify cathode‐Al redox chemistry as an internal heat‐amplification mechanism that should be considered in battery hazard assessment and high‐energy‐cell safety design.

title: Heterostructure Design in Two‐Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost‐efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one‐pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.

title: Rigid Double‐Spiro‐Grid Polymer Regulates Donor Fibrillar Pre‐Assembly and Acceptor Interdiffusion in Layer‐by‐Layer Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Layer‐by‐layer (LBL) fabrication of organic solar cells (OSCs) decouples donor and acceptor deposition, which, however, induces difficulties in controlling donor crystallization and acceptor interdiffusion. Here, we introduce NPSG, a fully conjugated double‐spiro‐grid polymer, to regulate donor fibrillar pre‐assembly before acceptor deposition. Morphological results reveal that NPSG shifts D18 assembly from loosely associated aggregates toward pronounced fibrillar pre‐assemblies in solution. Molecular dynamics simulations further suggest that the rigid NPSG backbone provides multiple noncovalent interaction sites that favor anisotropic association between D18 chain segments. During film formation, these fibrillar precursors evolve into a coherent and solvent‐resistant donor framework, which moderates L8‐BO interdiffusion and promotes a vertically graded, double fibrillar heterojunction. The resulting morphology facilitates interfacial charge transfer, improves the balance of electron and hole transport, and suppresses nongeminate recombination. Consequently, the optimized D18+NPSG/L8‐BO devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.2%, with a certified value of 20.7%. This strategy also improves device reproducibility, processing tolerance, applicability across different donor/acceptor systems, and operational stability under maximum‐power‐point (MPP) tracking. These findings establish donor‐underlayer pre‐assembly regulation as an effective strategy for efficient and robust sequentially processed OSCs.

title: Twistsonics: Engineering Acoustic Topological Textures in Moiré Sound Lattices
abstract: ABSTRACT Moiré superlattices formed by twisting periodic systems provide a powerful platform for emergent topological phenomena, but their use for programming real‐space topology in acoustic wave fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a phase‐controlled spoof surface acoustic wave platform for constructing moiré topological textures in the acoustic particle‐velocity field. On a perforated acoustic metasurface, two twisted skyrmion lattices are synthesized and superposed, yielding acoustic skyrmion bags with controllable topological numbers and geometries. The twist angle and rotation center control the scale and configuration of the bags, enabling deterministic reshaping of the composite texture. We further introduce controlled defects to assess the defect tolerance of the moiré skyrmion bags. The skyrmion bags retain their composite topology over a finite range of defect fractions, and comparison with an untwisted single‐layer skyrmion lattice suggests enhanced stability of the enclosed skyrmion cluster relative to the single‐layer reference at higher defect fractions. The same programmable platform also supports transitions from skyrmion lattices to meron lattices and enables twist‐induced meron clusters. These findings establish acoustic moiré superlattices as a reconfigurable platform for engineering robust real‐space topological textures, with potential applications in topology‐guided acoustic manipulation and information encoding.

title: Interface‐Directed Two‐Dimensional Growth of Non‐Layered NiO on MoS 2 Under Coupled External Fields
abstract: ABSTRACT The controlled growth of two‐dimensional (2D) non‐layered transition metal oxides remains a key challenge in low‐dimensional material synthesis. Achieving atomically precise construction of 2D structures requires a fundamental understanding of how external fields and interfacial interactions govern nucleation and growth processes. In this work, amorphous NiO x (a‐NiO x ) was deposited onto monolayer MoS 2 , and its transformation into crystalline 2D NiO nanosheets was directly visualized in situ using environmental transmission electron microscopy. The electron beam induces the decomposition of a‐NiO x into mobile NiO x species, which migrate and nucleate on MoS 2 , demonstrating the synergistic roles of the electron beam and thermal field in NiO cluster formation and interface‐dominated epitaxial growth. Combined notch‐filtered imaging and theoretical calculations reveal that Ni–O units preferentially attach at the NiO/MoS 2 interface to form one‐dimensional growth fronts, while oriented attachment proceeds via nanosheet rotation, interfacial fusion, and defect‐mediated reconstruction, culminating in lattice relaxation into a single‐crystalline structure. High‐throughput selected‐area electron diffraction further uncovers the modulation of external fields on the multi‐path structural evolution of NiO x . This work establishes an in situ strategy to resolve nucleation and growth pathways of 2D heterostructures, enabling active control over the 2D growth of non‐layered metal oxides and advancing deterministic atomic‐level construction.

title: Design of Heteroatomic Active Sites for Electrochemical CO x Reduction Toward Multicarbon Products
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical CO 2 and CO reduction (CO x RR) to value‐added multicarbon (C2+) products offers a promising route for sustainable carbon recycling and renewable fuel generation. Although Cu catalysts exhibit unique activity, these single‐metal sites are constrained by linear scaling relations of intermediate adsorption energies, which limits further improvements in selectivity and energy efficiency. Introducing heteroatoms to regulate active‐site coordination provides an effective approach to transcend these limitations. This review describes recent advances in the theoretical design, controllable fabrication, and mechanistic investigation of heteroatomic active sites for CO x RR toward C2+ products. Theoretical identification for high‐performance sites through descriptor‐based modeling, data‐driven screening, and dynamic simulations is first discussed. Then, the precision synthesis strategies for constructing atomically dispersed, long‐range‐ordered, and interfacial‐confined heteroatomic structures are systematically summarized. Subsequently, mechanistic insights into the promoting effect of heteroatoms, driven by synergistic electronic and geometric modulation, are highlighted, followed by an analysis of future research directions and the key challenges for the industrial implementation of heteroatomic catalysts for CO x RR. This review provides an integrated perspective linking active‐site design to catalytic performance, offering guidance for the development of next‐generation heteroatomic electrocatalysts for efficient CO x RR toward the sustainable production of high‐value chemicals.

title: Tailored Cationic Visible‐Light‐Active Interfaces for Sustainable, Biodegradable Nanofibers With Dual‐Mode Antimicrobial Activity and Robust Electrostatic Particle Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT The accumulation of microplastics originating from single‐use personal protective equipment presents a growing environmental concern. Developing biodegradable fibrous alternatives is essential, but integrating robust antimicrobial efficacy with stable electrostatic capture while maintaining degradability remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a surface co‐functionalization strategy addressing these challenges through covalent immobilization of sodium copper chlorophyllin (SCC) and quaternary ammonium compounds (QAC). Beyond simple dual functionalization, this molecular design induces intramolecular charge separation, suppressing electron‐hole recombination in SCC and thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species generation under visible light. Simultaneously, QAC introduce permanent cationic surface charges that enable contact‐mediated microbial inactivation and humidity‐resistant electrostatic particle capture. Demonstrated on biodegradable silk nanofibers as a model substrate, the functionalized fibers exhibit potent antibacterial and antiviral activity under both dark and illuminated conditions, together with high nanoparticle capture efficiency. Importantly, the fibers retain intrinsic biodegradability, undergoing near‐complete degradation under enzymatic conditions and substantial decomposition in soil environments. This work establishes a versatile surface functionalization platform applicable to diverse fibrous substrates, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional microplastic‐generating protective materials.

title: Surface‐Coordinated Gas–Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi‐2D Polyphenylacetylene Single‐Crystalline Nanoribbons
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular‐weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long‐range order. Here, we report a gas–solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi‐2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single‐crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuO x surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination‐assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π‐stacking‐driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer‐scale PPA single‐crystalline nanoribbons with left‐handed cis‐transoidal helical chains and long‐range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended‐chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper‐bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 10 9 g mol − 1 . The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W − 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 10 1 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade‐off between molecular‐weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi‐2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.

title: Ionization‐State‐Directed Sulfonate‐Rich Buried Interfaces Enable Durable High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton‐triggered degradation at the buried interface severely undermines the operational stability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, this work develops an ionization‐state‐directed sulfonate approach using sodium 2,2'‐disulfanediyldiethanesulfonate (DDANA). The pre‐deprotonated sulfonate terminals grant DDANA strong coordination with lead sites and drive its spontaneous aggregation at the perovskite and self‐assembled monolayer interface, forming robust multisite binding with the perovskite lattice. The enriched sulfonate groups build favorable interfacial dipoles to optimize energy level alignment and facilitate hole transport. The immobilized sulfonate groups act as conjugate‐based sites to competitively capture protons, while the disulfide skeleton enables reversible iodine‐redox to scavenge corrosive iodine species under operational stress. Dissociated sodium (Na + ) ions embed into lattice interstices and release residual tensile strain. As a result, DDANA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 27.38% (certified 27.13%). The strategy extends seamlessly to flexible devices and rigid large‐area modules, delivering efficiencies of 25.88% and 23.33%, respectively. Moreover, the DDANA‐modified devices retain 98.9% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking and 97.4% after cycling diurnals. This work establishes sulfonate ionization‐state engineering as a versatile molecular design platform for constructing chemically robust buried interfaces toward efficient, stable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
